# Decision Log

Append-only. Each entry records the date, the decision, its source (**U** = the user,
**R**n = `research/n`, **L** = lead agent proposal accepted by the user), and where it is
reflected. If a later decision supersedes an entry, mark the old one `superseded by Dn` and
never delete it.

## 2026-11-09: Server mode (overnight build)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D54 | **Remote access, first slice: server mode + code pairing.** (1) The main process runs on a Linux VPS as a systemd *user* service (`ducter service install`: `Restart=on-failure`, journald, linger, data in `~/.ducter`), bound to 127.0.0.1 unless `--host` says otherwise. (2) Off-machine clients pair once: `ducter pair` shows a one-time 8-character code (10 min, single use, unambiguous alphabet) with the address, a pasteable link and a QR; `POST /pair` trades it for a long-lived **device token**. Codes and tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes; wrong codes are rate limited; each device is revocable (`ducter devices disconnect`). (3) A request is *local* only if the peer and the Host are loopback and no proxy header is present; local clients stay token-free, everything else needs the token on `/ws`, and on `/mcp` beside the role token. (4) TLS is never hand-rolled: Caddy with automatic HTTPS on the user's own domain (Q18, `scripts/caddy-setup.sh`); an SSH tunnel is the zero-domain fallback. (5) The desktop gets **连接到你的 Ducter / Connect to your Ducter** (address + 配对码), token in a 0600 file. (6) Workers dial out to `/worker`; the main places tasks on them by `Place.device` (state stays on the main; the worker holds the place and runs the harness), and a worker that drops mid-task makes its tasks 在等 · <device> 连不上 after 2 min and resumes them by session id. Refines D40 (this is its code half; the WebCrypto device key + passkey and the Edge relay of D39/D46 remain the phone/web target). *Proposed overnight from the user's ask; accepted 2026-11-09 morning (U "按建议"); the code is shown as 连接码 / Code since D65* | U (ask) + L, R29 | `design/system.md`, `roadmap.md`, `design/onboarding.md`, `design/product-model.md` §1, `design/scenarios.md` |
| D55 | **Ducter.app is signed with the Nowledge Labs Developer ID and notarized**, the way con and Nowledge Mem ship. Bundle id `co.nowledge.ducter` (helper `co.nowledge.ducter.cli`), following `co.nowledge.con` and `co.nowledge.mem.desktop` (reverse DNS of nowledge.co); replaces the ad-hoc id `dev.ducter.app`. Hardened runtime on the app and helper; the helper's only entitlement is `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` (Bun's JIT dies without it, tested). App and DMG are both notarized and stapled; credentials use con/Mem's names (Apple ID + app-specific password, an API key, or a `notarytool` keychain profile). Ad-hoc signing stays the fallback without an identity | U (ask) | `scripts/make-app.sh`, README, `design/onboarding.md` |

## 2026-11-09: Morning decisions (the author's answers to the overnight list)

The author: "关闭窗口在后台会比较自然一些；词汇表你要仔细反思，不能有非人类感觉和无关的新概念，仔细看看；那些建议你自己第一性原理反思好按照建议吧". Each recommendation in `design/flows/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` was re-checked from first principles before it was recorded; where the check changed it, the entry says so.

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D56 | **Ducter keeps running when the window closes.** Closing the Ducter.app window leaves Ducter and its tasks working in the background, the way Mail or a chat app does; opening the app again reconnects. Quitting is an explicit act (Quit in the menu); how Ducter stays resident and what Quit does with running tasks follow the implementation, recorded in `design/onboarding.md`. Why: "silence means success" needs work to carry on when the user looks away; a window is a view, not the partner's life. Supersedes the overnight "Ducter lives as long as the app" default | U | `design/onboarding.md` app path, `README.md` |
| D57 | **Local trust: a local token, then no special case for loopback.** Today loopback stays token-free on single-user machines, and Ducter is not recommended on a shared host. Next: a 0600 local token in the data dir that the CLI, the same-machine desktop and the tasks' MCP config present automatically; once it exists, every caller shows a token, loopback included, and `DUCTER_LOCAL_TRUST` is retired. An SSH-tunnel client then connects once with a code like any other device. *Changed on reflection:* the recommendation was to switch `off` only when other human users exist; with an automatic local token the strict rule costs nothing, and one rule is simpler and honest everywhere ("only connected devices get in") | U ("按建议"), L | `design/system.md` "Who counts as local", `todo.md` |
| D58 | **The web client is `apps/web` (Preact), phone first.** It is served by the main process at `/app` and shares the desktop's i18n keys and Pebble tokens. Amends D20 for the web: MyGo native stays the desktop client; a MyGo WASM web client is dropped from the plan unless a need appears; Expo stays the later native app. *Changed on reflection:* the recommendation kept MyGo WASM "for a desktop-class web client later"; that would be a third UI codebase for no user need, so it is dropped | U ("按建议"), L | `design/system.md` Clients, `roadmap.md` |
| D59 | **Phone push defaults as built.** A decision unread for 30 s earns one push; pushes coalesce per 15 min; done results never push unless the user turns on 做完了也告诉我 / Also tell me when something's done; quiet hours default to 23:00–08:00 in the phone's time zone (免打扰), nothing breaks through (D52 Q12), at most one push when they end; iOS tap-to-open, Android adds Go / Hold. *Added on reflection:* coalescing must never hold a decision past its own default, so a decision whose default would fire before the coalescing window ends goes out at once (not built yet; `todo.md`) | U ("按建议"), L | `design/flows/D-decisions-attention.md`, `todo.md` |

| D72 | **The lifecycle loop of Ducter.app: updates, removal, help.** (1) **Updates: a small Go updater, not Sparkle** (`apps/desktop/internal/update`). Once at launch and daily it reads the newest published release of wey-gu/ducter through GitHub's public API, unauthenticated (a 404 while the repo is private is silence, not an error); downloads `Ducter-X-arm64.dmg` into Application Support, checks it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, copies the app out next to the running one and checks the copy (bundle id, version, `codesign --verify --deep --strict`, a Developer ID Application requirement of the running app's own team on app and helper, `spctl`). It never interrupts: one quiet line in the app menu (and Settings) "有新版本 0.2.0 · 重启时更新 / Update 0.2.0 ready · restart to finish"; the next quit installs it (default on), or Restart now. The swap happens after the app exits (rename; the previous version kept for a rollback; the old one put back if the new can't move in), then the background LaunchAgent is restarted so Ducter runs the new helper and resumes from the Log. Why not Sparkle: an Objective-C framework to embed and sign into a Go app built without Xcode, plus an EdDSA key and appcast to keep; the Developer ID team check already proves who built it (Apple issues and revokes the certificate) and the release already carries checksums. Why not mygo's own updater: it wants its own archive format and key, and checks neither the team nor Gatekeeper. (2) **彻底移除 Ducter / Remove Ducter**: a page listing exactly what goes (the LaunchAgent, `~/.ducter` with the Log, task working copies and browser profiles, the app's `~/.local/bin/ducter` link, its Library folders) and what stays (repos and their `ducter/*` branches, Claude Code / Codex logins, Nowledge Mem, cua-driver); "only stop and remove the background item" or "remove everything" (typed confirmation; uncommitted task changes named first; stops if a Ducter started in Terminal still runs); the app goes to the Trash last. The CLI owns the list (`ducter uninstall [--all]`), so app, terminal and server remove the same things. (3) **Reset partner is not built**: the Log is one append-only file for the conversation *and* every task (principle 1), so cutting the conversation out would orphan tasks, decisions and resume; the safe form is a "new conversation" boundary event the projection starts after, which is a context-design change (`design/todo.md`). ## 2026-11-09: Where keys live (security review: D85's env file reached every harness)

DRAFT, for the author's review. D97–D101 are held by the proposals in `design/connectors.md`.

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D102 | **Every secret lives in a 0600 file in the data folder and is read only by the code that uses it; no key enters a process environment wholesale.** (1) Harness keys and login tokens (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, …) live in `<dataDir>/keys.env` (0600, `KEY=value`). A server's systemd unit never loads it; its `EnvironmentFile` stays `<dataDir>/env`, for non-secret settings only. Connection tokens stay in `connection-tokens.json` (D96). (2) Upgrade: on every start (core, worker) and on `ducter service install`, secret-shaped lines in `<dataDir>/env` move to `keys.env` (a value already there wins), other lines stay, both files are tightened to 0600; idempotent. Keys a unit already loaded are dropped from Ducter's own environment. ## 2026-11-09: Work over time, built (the author's "针对用户的长时间 loop 的 focus window 或者语义的等待条件…我记得我提及过这个需求"; reviews of prototype v1–v5)

DRAFT, for the author's review. D103–D111 are held by other branches. Prototype:
https://claude.ai/artifact/CMBoqncshR96q9fzgUhpXy (v5).

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D112 | **A waiter waits for a condition, not only a time; Ducter on its bench is what waiting looks like.** (1) Kinds: **timer** (`wait_until`); **check**: the condition compiled into one read-only command (argv, never a shell line) and a predicate on its exit code or output (`gh pr checks 1592 --json state`, every `state` is SUCCESS), run on the task's device in its place with an allowlisted environment, no model per look; only reading forms are allowed (gh view/checks/list and GET `api`, curl GET/HEAD with no body, output file, config or credentials, git ls-remote/log/status/rev-parse/describe, test, stat, ls, cat, head, tail, wc, grep, `nc -z`, `ping -c`, dig, host, date, pgrep), never a key or credential file; **event**: new items from the user's OpenConnector Provider Trigger (D96, connectors.md §4.5) with the checkpoint kept in the Log; **judge**: a check or event plus a yes/no question a cheap model answers over what was fetched, only when that changed and at most once per 10 minutes. (2) Every 5 minutes by default (60 s floor); errors back off by doubling to 30 minutes; a look is logged only when what it saw changed. (3) A deadline (`until`) ends it as `expired`: a task's wait puts the task on needs-you and the partner is told (focus-window-states.md). (4) A task's own wait (`wait_for` in the task's tools, or the partner's with a taskId) rests the task on Waiting and wakes the task, not the partner, when it holds. (5) Everything is rebuilt from the Log; armed waits look again soon after a restart. (6) The reason names what is awaited (等 PR #1592 通过), never as done. (7) **What waiting looks like:** Ducter's sixth pose, sitting on a little bench looking out, with a small cream bubble holding the clay thing it waits for (a PR, a cloud for CI and anything online, an envelope, a clock, a file). Objects alone were tested first and rejected: the mailbox already means a connected account, the lighthouse an ability, the jetty pairing; the hourglass read as loading (3/5), the float as bait or a scam (3/5). No pose alone reached 9/10 with LLM-proxy raters (chin on hands 1–2/10 "thinking", a sign 1/10, the bench 5/10), so the words always say exactly what; the picture must not mislead. A round with real people, children included, is still owed | U, L, R20 | `design/product-model.md` §4, `design/focus-window-states.md`, `packages/protocol/src/checks.ts`, `packages/core/src/waiters.ts` |
| D113 | **`until` on a task: keep going until the condition holds.** After each of the task's turns (its report) the condition is judged: by its compiled check when it has one, else by the cheap judge over the report. Not yet: the next try ("第 n 次：…还没做到") starts by itself. It stops on the condition, 20 tries (default), 3 tries without progress, or going in circles (an observation coming back after a different one); short of the condition the task goes to needs-you and the partner says so once. While it runs, a try's own done report neither finishes the task nor shows as a result; the loop's end is the result. | D114 | **Routines (例行) are built as D29 says**, with these choices: created only by `routine_propose`, which writes a proposal card (a decision with `routineId`, default Hold, never reversible); Go activates it, Hold dismisses it. Time triggers (day, weekday, week, month, every n hours) in the user's zone (personal: the latest zone a client reports in `hello`) or a pinned one (world); condition triggers reuse D112's waits and fire on the change to true, then re-arm. Each firing opens a fresh task with the routine's brief, its effect scope and report policy written into it; a run still going makes the next firing a skip. Missed firings coalesce into one late run within min(period/2, 12 h), else one recorded skip. Per run, at most 2× the first run's tokens (the run is interrupted past it); a monthly cap pauses it. It pauses itself after 3 failed runs, 3 unread reports, the month's cap, or its review date (30 days; then "还要吗？/ Keep this?"); the partner may pause one; only the user resumes. Runner-up rejected: routines inside Waiting (the lane would never empty). No ticking numbers; nothing moves on its own; with reduced motion all of it is still. (3) The mechanism stays off every default surface: cards, the opened task's head, the proposal card and the conversation never say how often it looks, which command, or whether a model judges. ## 2026-11-09: Ack and go (the author: "接活时候并行先回一句并行启动 focus window")

DRAFT, for the author's review. D112–D119 are held for other branches (work-over-time may use D112+), so this is D120.

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D120 | **Ack and go: one sentence at once, the task starting with it.** (1) Work that becomes a task gets **one** short sentence in the user's language: the action (never its outcome), that the partner will say when it's clear, and a rough usual duration **only when something grounds it** (a similar task here took that long, the repo's size, how long its CI runs): zh 「一般」「大概」, en "usually", "about", never a promise; no grounds, no number. Then nothing until the result. An ask it can't act on without guessing gets one short question instead. (2) The sentence ends the waiting line (the partner sends `activity: null` with the ack, and no "Setting up a task…" flashes before it); the header's **在做 1 件 / 1 under way** follows from the task's card. (3) **The task does not wait for its brief.** `task_open` takes title, then place, then brief; the runner's normalizer emits the call's head (the fields before `"brief"`) as it streams, and `Runner.openTaskEarly` makes the card, the place and the session from the title (when the user's words name the place) or the head; the brief becomes the session's first turn and is logged as a second `task_open`. An early task whose place or AI the head or the call contradicts, or whose call never comes, is dropped before it did anything (reason `not started`, never in the partner's task list), and the right one opens. Recovery reads the latest `task_open` and never starts an unbriefed task. (4) Finished tasks show "took about N min" in the partner's task list, as grounds for the next estimate. Measured live (one run each, warm session, zh request, scratch repo): sonnet ack 1.2 s, task session spawn 1.8 s (before: 1.2 s / 4.7–5.1 s); opus ack 2.3 s, spawn 3.0 s (before: 2.1 s / 7.5 s). Partner eval subset (14): sonnet 10 → 14, haiku 9 → 14; full sonnet 54/55 | U, L | `packages/partner/src/{persona,partner,render}.ts`, `packages/runner/src/{normalize,runner,brief}.ts`, `design/quiet-conversation.md`, `design/conversation.md` |

## 2026-11-09: The conversation's own memory, built (AGENTS.md build state: "The memory digest is built, with its eval suite")

DRAFT, for the author's review. Numbered D123 at merge (D122 went to oo).

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D123 | **D7 is built, with these choices.** (1) Frozen digests live in the Log's own SQLite file, in an append-only table (`spine`, triggers refuse UPDATE and DELETE), not as channel events, so clients never receive them; migration 1 adds it. (2) A segment closes past 24K of unsummarized tail (cut where it is 16–24K, at a turn boundary, best with no open ask straddling it, after a pause or a task result), after a merge or PR by button (a finished topic, ≥ 4K), or after 2 h quiet (≥ 4K); never after the user's own message. On first use at most 10 segments' worth of history is digested. (3) The writer is a tool-less background session on the partner's harness with a mid-tier model (`sonnet` on Claude Code), never awaited by a turn. The model writes TOC, decisions, Superseded, anchors, soft obligations and the narrative; **code** opens and closes every obligation it can see (a running task, an open question, an armed timer), writes the task snapshot and assigns the ids. (4) The audit gates every freeze; a failure is rewritten with the reasons, then repaired by removal only, then replaced by a degraded mechanical index; nothing that failed freezes. (5) Epochs roll up 8 of 16+ segments by concatenation and carry every task's last state (the first fake run lost "which tasks did we open" without it). (6) A fresh session reads `<earlier_conversation>` `<open_items>` `<conversation_so_far>` (lines with `#seq`) `<tasks>`; the window is 8–24K; a warm session past 120K re-cuts (the harness's own count, the estimate as fallback; wording corrected 2026-11-09). (7) `log_search` ranks by reciprocal-rank fusion of BM25 over CJK bigrams, exact substrings and recency, the user's words ×1.15; no vectors yet. (8) Automatic pre-turn recall is built and **off**: it fires only on recall intent and admitted 5 of 8 hits correctly on the eval corpus, under the 0.8 bar. (9) Measured on a week-long zh/en corpus (11 question types, rule-graded, 31 probes, Sonnet writer, Haiku answerer, search for every condition): full transcript 1.00 / 1.00, verbatim window alone 0.87 / 0.77, the spine 0.97 / 0.97 (runs 2 and 3; run 1 found an audit bug and a grading bug, run 3 one more grading bug, all fixed with tests and noted in the reports); false memory 0 and stale assertions 0 in all three after re-grading. The spine's remaining miss is a rationale the writer kept only as "防篡改" (d2). The corpus is ~2K tokens at budgets scaled 50× down: it shows what is kept, not compression | L, R14, R15 | `design/memory.md` "as built", `packages/partner/src/spine/`, `packages/core/src/{log,spine}.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/search.ts`, `packages/partner/eval/memory/`, `packages/partner/eval/results/2026-11-09-memory-*.md` |

(3) **Start** opens the task at once with the words verbatim as its brief (no partner rewrite), then opens that task (Esc returns). Title = the first sentence, about 24 Chinese characters or 48 letters, cut with "…"; the partner may retitle it once after the first report (task_retitle). (4) **The Log** records task_open with `origin: "you"` (the card shows `openedBy: "you"`); nothing appears in the conversation at open time (only the counters change). The partner reads a hidden note, 你自己开了「X」/ You opened "X" yourself (a user-origin `body_<task>_opened` job_status, hidden in every client, never waking it), and its task list marks the task; it reports the result like any task (D124). Core counts the diff (files, lines added and removed since the branch left its base, committed or not) after each turn, report and state change, caches it, and puts it on the card (`changes`); On hand never waits for git. (6) **Not in it:** no tabs, no model or effort picker, no pin or search. Attachments wait (todo, trigger: the first time a brief needs a screenshot). (7) **So a lead agent can work Ducter without the author relaying:** `ducter say "<words>"` (a user message over the client protocol, exactly as an app sends it; prints the partner's words as they arrive, ends when its turn settles, `--timeout`; prints any decision it raised with its id), `ducter tail [task]` (the conversation, or one task's steps one line each, as text; Ctrl-C stops), `ducter answer <id or part of the question> go\|hold\|"<reply>"`, and `ducter open <part of a title or id>` (the connected apps show it through a new `open_task` frame; with none, it says where the task is). ## 2026-11-09: Native browser and computer use by default (research/38 follow-up)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D130 | **Native browser and computer use are the default; cua-driver is the fallback (supersedes D126's "the default stays cua-driver").** Decided by the author (2026-11-09): "这才能最大利用 codex 优势". (1) **Codex tasks keep Codex's own Computer Use and browser use**, in every place. Ducter's clean setup for a task keeps plugins on as a feature, turns off by id every plugin the user enabled except `browser`, `chrome`, `unified-computer-use` and `computer-use` (all `@openai-bundled`), keeps the desktop app's `node_repl` server, and leaves `computer_use` / `browser_use` on; the partner's clean setup is unchanged (`features.plugins=false`). The plugin id goes in bare: `-c plugins.<id>.enabled=false` (verified against `mcpServerStatus/list`, codex-cli 0.167.0; the quoted form research/38 tried is not matched). A browser place on Codex uses that clean setup: only `cua_repl` and `node_repl` carry tools (~400 `codex_apps` tools and the user's own cua-driver left out). Codex's DOM-level browser tools (in-app browser, Chrome via the ChatGPT extension) are used when the desktop app's browser access host reaches Ducter (its three `BROWSER_USE_ACCESS_*` env vars, passed through to Codex); Ducter never reads them from another process. Otherwise Codex drives Chrome as an app through Computer Use. (2) **Claude Code tasks prefer Claude in Chrome** (`--chrome`), checked at task open: a live local bridge socket (`/tmp/claude-mcp-browser-bridge-<user>/<pid>.sock`), else one read-only `list_connected_browsers` call to `claude --claude-in-chrome-mcp` (no model call, ~2 s, reused 30 s). Not connected: cua-driver. A task that still meets "Browser extension is not connected" moves to cua-driver in place (same session resumed, a system line says so). (3) **cua-driver is the fallback** (pi, DeepSeek Harness, a harness whose own tools aren't ready); `DUCTER_BROWSER_DRIVER=cua` forces it. `DEFAULT_BROWSER_DRIVER = native`. ## 2026-11-10: A folder that isn't a repo works in place and is undone with one tap (the author: "第一性原理建议就好，go")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D142 | **A task in a non-git folder (Documents, Downloads, a folder of invoices) works in the folder itself; Ducter keeps a copy from before, says what changed in plain words, and puts it all back with one tap.** Supersedes D27's draft copy, its apply Go and "trusted folders". (1) **The copy:** before a task's first turn (and again after the user kept or undid), the runner copies the folder to `<dataDir>/snapshots/<taskId>/copy` on the machine that holds it: an APFS clone on macOS (`cp -c -R -p`, verified on this Mac's data volume) or `cp -a --reflink=always` on btrfs/xfs, near-zero space and time; a plain copy only up to 256 MB (`DUCTER_SNAPSHOT_COPY_MAX_MB`) and on a different volume or file system; nothing past 100k entries. (2) **Ask first instead** (the runner holds the turn and logs a needs_input report, Hold by default, not reversible) when the folder can't be copied cheaply: cloud-synced (iCloud Drive and its Desktop & Documents xattr, `~/Library/CloudStorage` for Dropbox / Google Drive / OneDrive / Box, the old home-folder sync folders, a `.dropbox` marker), on a network or external drive, too big, or holding Ducter's own data. Go or a reply sends the held turn and it doesn't ask again for that task. (3) **Changes in plain words:** counted against the copy (added, changed, removed; a removed and an added file with the same bytes are one move, a rename when the folder is the same), cached on the card (`TaskCard.folder`) and carried on done and failed reports (`report.folder`), so the partner's result says it can be undone and until when. The opened task's Changes is one sentence (**把 42 个文件整理进 6 个新文件夹，改了 3 个文件名 / Moved 42 files into 6 new folders, renamed 3**), a quiet **随时能改回去，留到 11 月 16 日 / You can undo this until Nov 16**, then **改回去 / Undo all changes** and **就这样 / Keep the changes**; the list on request (**看看改了哪些 / See what changed**) with **改回这个 / Undo this** per file. No Merge for a folder. The mechanism is never named. (4) **Undo** makes the folder exactly what the copy holds (removes what the task added, puts back the rest with clones, times and modes) and checks it: no entry differs, and every file put back has the copy's hash; then the copy is freed. A folder changed after the task finished asks first and says what would be lost (**它做完之后，又有 1 个文件被改过（…）**, **还是改回去 / Undo anyway**). Not while the task works there. (5) **Kept 7 days** after the task last finished (done, failed or dropped), swept hourly; **就这样** frees it at once. (6) **What is enforced, what is detected:** Codex folder tasks run in its workspace-write sandbox (Ducter's `-c sandbox_mode="workspace-write"` after OAR's own wins, checked with `codex app-server` config/read; `codex sandbox` refused a write in the home folder; network on). Claude Code under bypass has no switch that keeps writes in a folder (its own sandbox wasn't verified here), so for it staying inside the folder and asking before deleting more than 10 files at once are asked in the brief, not enforced. Inside the folder everything is undoable either way, deletions included; writes outside it are not covered by the copy. (7) Protocol: `FolderSummary`/`FolderChanges`/`UndoConfirm`; `task_action` `undo` (`path`, `force`) and `keep`, answered with `action_result` (`confirm`); `folder_changes` both ways; `SessionSpec.confineWrites`; worker ops `folderPrepare/Finish/Changes/Undo/Keep` (an older worker can't copy, so its tasks ask first). CLI `ducter undo <task> [--yes]`. Git repos keep the worktree and Merge (D26) | U (2026-11-09), L | `packages/runner/src/folder.ts`, `runner.ts`, `brief.ts`, `oar.ts`, `remote.ts`, `worker-host.ts`, `tools.ts`, `packages/core/src/{changes,ws,main}.ts`, `packages/partner/src/render.ts`, `packages/protocol`, `packages/cli`, `apps/desktop`, `apps/web`, `design/product-model.md` §3, `design/flows/EC-steering-places.md` C2, `design/focus-window.md`, `docs/privacy-and-safety.md` |
| D143 | **A server reaches the world through `ducter domain <name>`, and every printed command works in the shell it was printed in.** (1) `ducter domain` replaces copying `scripts/caddy-setup.sh` by hand: Ducter must answer locally; the name's A/AAAA records must include this server's public IP (api.ipify.org; else it prints the exact record and stops; `--no-dns-check` skips); nothing but Caddy may hold 80/443 (else `--print` for the proxy the user keeps); Caddy is installed (apt as root without sudo, sudo otherwise; Homebrew on a Mac); one marked block (`# ducter: begin` … `# ducter: end`) goes into the Caddyfile (the Debian demo site moved aside); then HTTPS is waited for (60 s), `public-url` written, and a pair code shown. Idempotent; `--remove` takes only Ducter's block out; `--json` for agents (steps, error, next). (2) `ducter pair` on a server with no address leads with the domain path and the public IP, then the SSH tunnel for a Mac alone; it no longer waits there, and `--json` carries `reachable`, `publicIp`, `tunnel`, `steps`. No user-facing text names `caddy-setup.sh`. (3) Installers: as root (or with a writable `/usr/local/bin`) link `/usr/local/bin/ducter`; otherwise one marked PATH block in the shell's profile plus the export line for this shell; commands print as `ducter` only when PATH finds this binary, else its path. (4) `uninstall --all` also removes that link, that block, the binary `install.sh` copied, and Ducter's Caddy site (Caddy stays). (5) `skills/` ships Agent Skills (ducter-deploy, -operate, -troubleshoot), served at `ducter.ai/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | U (2026-11-10), L | `packages/cli/src/{domain,remote,uninstall,main}.ts`, `scripts/install.sh`, `apps/site/public/install.sh`, `scripts/caddy-setup.sh`, `skills/`, `docs/install.md`, `docs/for-agents.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `design/build-and-run.md` |

## 2026-11-10: The command line follows the Ducter you use (the lead: once the Mac app connected to hel.siwei.info, `ducter status` on the Mac still showed the stale local Ducter)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D147 | **`ducter` on a computer talks to the same Ducter the user uses there; only commands about the machine itself stay local.** (1) **Two kinds of command:** machine commands (`up`, `service`, `uninstall`, `worker`, `doctor`, `domain`, `report`, `update` without `--all`) always act on this computer; home commands (`status`, `say`, `task`, `tail`, `answer`, `merge`, `undo`, `open`, `pair`, `devices`, `update --all`) go to the Ducter the command line follows. (2) **What it follows:** `<dataDir>/home.json` (0600: `{address, token, name, since, deviceId?, by}`), else this computer's Ducter. The Mac app writes it when it connects elsewhere: over its own authenticated socket it asks the home for a second one-time code (the existing `pair_code` frame; no new endpoint) and redeems it as a separate device **CLI on <Mac>**, so the command line is revocable on its own and never holds the app's token. Switching the app back to this Mac removes the file. Without the app, `ducter connect <address> --code <code>` writes it and `ducter disconnect` removes it; at launch the app leaves a file the user wrote that way alone, and re-pairs only a CLI token that stopped working. If the app can't pair the CLI (an older home), the file still names the address without a token, so commands say the exact `ducter connect` line instead of quietly showing this Mac. (3) **Always visible:** every home command prints `→ hel.siwei.info` / `→ this computer` first and carries `home` in `--json`; `--local` (or an explicit `--port`) forces this computer, `--home <address>` goes elsewhere once (a token is needed: else the connect line). (4) **Transport:** the client WebSocket over `wss://…/ws` with `Authorization: Bearer dvc.…`, as the phone and the app. Failures say what to do: unreachable → check the server; the gate's 401 → it was disconnected there, connect again with a new code. `devices disconnect` stays on the home's own machine (no remote revoke frame yet). (5) **A task from the CLI** while following a server has no folder unless `--repo` names one (then on this Mac as its device, which works when this Mac does tasks for it). ## 2026-11-10: Every device updates in place, and its card says so (the author: "in-place update is a basic capability"; "每一个卡片也应该优雅设计")

DRAFT, for the author's review.

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D148 | **Ducter's home and every other computer update in place from the official release, one tap or `ducter update`, with a check before and a rollback after; each device card says its version, renames in place and disconnects with a confirm.** (1) **Knowing.** Every device reports its version: the home in `/health` (`version` beside `build`, local callers only) and in its devices frame, a worker in its hello. The home reads `api.github.com/repos/wey-gu/ducter/releases/latest` (else the `releases/latest` redirect, which gives the version but no notes), at most every 6 h, cached in `<dataDir>/updates/latest.json`; offline or refused stays silent and keeps the last answer; `DUCTER_UPDATE_CHECK=off` never asks. Drafts and pre-releases are never offered. Each device in the devices frame carries `update {current, latest, available, notes, security, how, phase …}`; `notes` is the release notes' first two plain lines. (2) **How it updates (`how`).** `self`: a compiled Linux `ducter` in a folder it can write (the server bundle) updates itself. `app`: a Mac whose `ducter` lives inside Ducter.app updates through the app's own updater (D72; that bundle swap is the app's, not this decision's): on that Mac the button calls the app's update, elsewhere the card says to update from Ducter on that Mac. `source`: run from a checkout, updated with git. Nothing else. (3) **The staged update** (`packages/core/src/update.ts`, one code path for the home, a worker and `ducter update`): refuse a downgrade unless `--to <version>` names it; refuse when the staging disk has less than 3× the download free; download `ducter-<v>-linux-<arch>.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` from `github.com/wey-gu/ducter/releases/download/v<v>/` over HTTPS only (redirects only to GitHub's own hosts); the SHA-256 must match the listed sum or nothing is changed; unpack into `<dataDir>/updates/<v>/`; self-check the new binary (`--version` must name `<v>`, `doctor --json` in a scratch folder must print its checks); keep the running binary as `ducter.prev` beside it; move the new one in by rename (same folder, atomic). (4) **Safe point.** Before a restart it waits until no merge, undo, keep or archive is running (the runner's critical section; new ones are refused with a plain line meanwhile) and gives tasks mid-turn up to 2 min to end their turn; a task still mid-turn then is resumed by the restart's recovery, as after any restart. (5) **Restart and rollback.** The restart runs from a helper outside the service (`systemd-run --user` with the previous binary, `ducter update --finish`), so it survives `systemctl --user restart ducter`. It waits up to 60 s for the new process to be healthy (the home: `/health` names the new version; a worker: it reached its main and wrote `updates/alive`). Not healthy: it moves `ducter.prev` back, restarts again, and records the failure with its reason. Without systemd it swaps and says to restart. (6) **Seen.** Every step goes to the Log (`device_update` on the `devices` stream: downloading, checking, waiting, restarting, done or failed with reason and `rolledBack`), and the outcome file is read after the restart, so a client that reconnects sees **回来了，现在是 {v} / Back, now on {v}**. (7) **Workers.** The home sends `update` down the worker's socket; the worker runs the same staged update for its own binary and service, reports each phase up the same socket, comes back and says its new version in its hello. A Mac worker inside Ducter.app answers `app`. (8) **CLI.** `ducter update` (this machine), `--all` (workers first, then the home), `--check` (only report), `--json`, `--yes`, `--to <v>`. Agents run `ducter update --check --json`, then `ducter update --yes`. (9) **UI.** No nagging: a device that's behind gets one quiet dot by its name and a line in its card, **有新版本 {v} / Update to {v}** with the first lines of what's new, and one button **更新 / Update**. Progress in words: **在下载… / Downloading… · 在核对… / Checking… · 等手头的事停好… / Waiting for work to settle… · 在重启… / Restarting… · 回来了，现在是 {v} / Back, now on {v}**; failed: **没更新成，已经换回 {old} / Didn't update; back on {old}** with the reason. The partner says one line only when asked, or for a release whose notes name a security fix. Settings › About lists the home's and each computer's version. (10) **At night** (setting `autoUpdate`, off by default): inside quiet hours, when no task is working and nothing is critical, the home updates itself, then each worker. (11) **Device cards** (desktop Devices, phone Settings; *the card's shape amended by D161*): one header (the name, renamed in place by clicking it: Enter saves, Esc cancels, through `rename_device`), what it is in plain words (**云上的电脑 · {name} 住这儿 / A computer in the cloud · {name} lives here**), a short state line, its AI accounts as coins (accounts not installed fold into **+ 再登录一个 AI / + Sign in another AI** unless none is signed in), abilities, the version line with the dot, and the actions at the bottom: **断开 / Disconnect** with a confirm (`disconnect_device`, the same revoke as `ducter devices disconnect`), never a terminal line in the UI. A phone or another window gets the same card: rename, last seen, disconnect | U ("in-place update is a basic capability", "每一个卡片也应该优雅设计"), L | `design/system.md`, `design/product-model.md`, `docs/install.md`, `docs/devices.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `skills/ducter-deploy`, `skills/ducter-operate`, `packages/core/src/{update,release}.ts`, `packages/cli/src/update.ts`, `apps/desktop`, `apps/web` |

The Log keeps the key (the task was given it to use it; the Log stays on the home); clients hide again at render (`packages/protocol/src/redact.ts`, its Go port `apps/desktop/internal/redact`, one fixture). No tap-to-reveal: the user who pasted it has it. (2) **One meta line**: the state, **one clock** (since it started, ticking until it finishes, then **用了 {duration} / took {duration}**; never a wall-clock time beside a step), then the agent's coin, the agent and model, where it runs when there is a place (repo · branch, a folder, **在 {device} 上 / on {device}** when it isn't this machine; no place says nothing), and **换谁来做 / Switch who does it** as a small action. The bar over the composer and the **细节 / Details** table go: who and where are the meta line, saved progress is in the transcript once, usage and the compaction count are not shown (D121's word count of cumulative tokens, cache reads included, read as noise); what went out stays as **发出去的 / Sent out** under the transcript when anything did; a wait's **怎么判断的 / How it checks** stays when there is a wait. Header actions per state: **先停 / Pause** while it works, **放下 / Drop** until it finishes. (3) **你交代的事 / What you asked** (or **{name} 交代的事 / What {name} asked**): the brief as a quiet sunken card, three lines until **展开 / Show all**. (4) **The agent's voice is the readable layer**: its messages and its saved progress (a checkpoint said once; when it repeats the message just before, that message gets the small **保存了进度 / Progress saved** mark) in body ink at the reading measure. (5) **Steps fold per stretch**: the steps between two things the agent said are one gist line, **查看了一圈 / Looked around** (only reading, searching, probing, requesting) · **改了 n 个文件 / Edited n files** · **在 {app} 里操作 / Worked in {app}** · **跑了几条命令 / Ran commands** · **想了想 / Thought it through**, then **· n 步 / n steps** and **· n 处出错 / n failed**; folded when settled, open while it is the stretch under way, whose gist is its latest step with a spinner. A lone step is its own line. A real failure shows even folded. (6) **A step is one sentence**: the agent's own words for it when its harness carries them (Claude Code's Bash `description`, Codex's `justification`), else the summarizer: `command -v nmem` → **查找 nmem 命令 / Looked for nmem**, `curl https://cloud.nowledge.co/…` → **请求 cloud.nowledge.co / Requested cloud.nowledge.co**, `curl … \| sh` → **运行 {host} 的安装脚本**, `pipx install x` → **安装 x / Installed x**, `python3 -c` → **运行一段 python3**, `mkdir` → **新建文件夹 x**; else the command's name and subcommand in mono after **运行 / Ran**. (7) **A probe that finds nothing is not an error**: `command -v`, `which`, `type`, `test` / `[`, `ls`, `grep` / `rg` exiting non-zero say **没找到 nmem / No nmem here** · **还没有 x / No x yet** · **没搜到 x / No match for x** in muted ink; only a real failure is the red **出错 / Error** line. (8) **Waiting on you with nothing to answer** (its turn ended on a question in its own words, or a wait ran out) reads **说完了，等你回话 / Over to you** with **它停在这儿了。回它一句，它就接着做。 / It stopped here. (11) **A pending ask sits over the composer**, where the answer is typed; an answered one is one line in the head. While it works, a reader at the end of the page follows the newest step; one who scrolled up stays. The agent's words stay in its own language (no silent translation; a translate action is in `todo.md`). The model is one table for both surfaces (`packages/protocol/src/transcript.ts`, its Go port, `fixtures/transcript.json`). ## 2026-11-10: One computer, one card, and a Mac that does tasks for a server

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D155 | **One computer, one card; every device card in D148's language; and one tap makes a Mac do tasks for a home elsewhere.** (1) **The command line belongs to its computer** (*how the card shows it amended by D161 (5)*). The CLI token the app pairs (D147) or `ducter connect` makes stays its own revocable device; only the presentation folds. `/pair` takes `form` (`"cli"` \| `"app"`) and `computer` (the host it runs on), kept in `devices.db` and sent as `reach.clients[].form/computer` and `devices[].computer`; a CLI paired before this is known by its name `CLI on <host>`. In the app (and the phone's Settings), a CLI folds into the worker or the app window on its computer as one quiet line **命令行也连着 / The command line is connected too** with its own **⋯ › 断开** (confirm: **断开 {host} 上的命令行？**); an app window folds into a worker on its computer (**Ducter app 也连着**). A CLI alone shows as a computer named after its host (**一台电脑 · 命令行连着**), never "CLI on …". (2) **Every card speaks plainly and renames** (*the card's words amended by D161 (1)–(4)*). Phones and windows get D148's card: name renamed in place (`rename_device` already handled clients; now tested), what it is (**你的 iPhone · 用 Safari 连着**, **一台 Mac · 用 Ducter app 连着**), now or last seen, **它能为你做的** (phones: notifications, answers, talk), the folded lines, then 断开 after a hairline. The home renames too: a display name in `<dataDir>/device-name`; it still answers to its host name and `local`, and never takes a paired device's name. A default name a live device of the same kind already has gets ` · 2`, ` · 3` at pairing. (3) **Let this Mac do tasks for {home}** (*on the card, D161's first chip*). With the app connected elsewhere, this Mac's card and Settings › 在哪儿运行 carry one switch. On: a code over the app's own socket (`pair_code`), redeemed with `role: "worker"`; `<dataDir>/worker.json` (0600); the bundled helper's `ducter worker` under the LaunchAgent `<bundle>.worker` (RunAtLoad, KeepAlive on an unclean exit, `<dataDir>/worker.log`, no token in the plist). Off: booted out and removed, `worker.json` gone, the worker revoked with `disconnect_device`. A worker only does tasks (`/worker`, `/mcp`), never the conversation. `ducter service install --worker` on a Mac writes the same LaunchAgent (`status`/`uninstall --worker` too); a refused worker exits 0 under launchd (`DUCTER_SUPERVISOR=launchd`) so it isn't restarted. Browser and computer use on such a Mac stay the home's only (roadmap). (4) **The Devices page is one scroll:** the stage keeps the window's height and stays in view (sticky), the card and what can be added flow at their natural height beside it; no nested scroller, no clipped first line, ability labels wrap to three lines | U ("CLI on … 这是啥", "右边卡片很丑而且不能改名", "怎么让这台 Mac 替 hel 做事", the nested scrollers), L | `packages/core/src/{auth,devices}.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/cli/src/{home,worker,remote,i18n}.ts`, `apps/desktop/{main.go,internal/local/{agent,worker}.go,internal/remote,internal/views/{computers,devicecard,devupdate,abilities,isles,settings_panels}.go,internal/i18n/computers.go}`, `apps/web/src/views.tsx`, `design/system.md`, `design/product-model.md`, `design/roadmap.md`, `docs/devices.md`, `docs/install.md` |

## 2026-11-10: Ducter knows each AI agent's version and updates it gracefully (the author: "on a server, and every computer, Ducter should know the versions of the AI agents it uses and upgrade them gracefully and automatically")

DRAFT, for the author's review.

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D156 | **Every device knows the version of each AI agent on it and where that copy came from, and updates it with the agent's own updater at a safe point, read back and rolled back where the channel can pin; at night only to versions Ducter verified.** (1) **Know.** Each device's AI agents carry `version` (its own `--version`), `how` it was installed, decided by where its binary really lives: `npm` (a global npm package; the prefix it lives under is kept), `brew` (a Homebrew cask), `installer` (the agent's own installer: Claude Code's native `~/.local/share/claude/versions`, Codex's standalone, pi's managed install), `app` (a copy inside the Codex app or the Claude app), `ducter` (pi inside Ducter from a checkout), `unknown` (a pnpm, yarn or bun global, anything else). The home reads `latest` from **that copy's own channel** (npm registry, Homebrew's cask API, the installer's own release pointer, pi.dev), one read per channel, at most every 6 h, kept in `<dataDir>/updates/agents-latest.json`, silent offline, `DUCTER_UPDATE_CHECK=off` never asks, never in tests. Workers send `version` and `how` in their hello; the home reads their channels. Each agent also carries `standing` (the installed version against harness-facts' verified range) and `latestVerified`. The per-agent facts (npm package, cask, installer mark, update and pin commands, app marks) are harness-facts' `channels`, the one registry (D135). (2) **Show** (*amended by D161 (3): in the coin's detail; the card shows one dot*). In the device card's AI account rows: **版本 {v} / Version {v}** quietly; behind: one dot and **有新版本 {v} / Update to {v}** with **更新 / Update**; outside the verified range: **Ducter 还没验证过这个版本。/ Ducter hasn't checked this version yet.** (honest, not alarming); a latest outside it: **Ducter 还没验证过 {v}，要等你点一下才装。/ Ducter hasn't checked {v} yet, so it waits for your tap.**; an app's copy: **随 Codex app 更新 / Updates with the Codex app** and no button; pi inside Ducter: **随 Ducter 更新 / Updates with Ducter**. (3) **Update** (`agent_update`, `packages/core/src/agents.ts`): wait until no task turn on that agent and no partner turn on it runs on that device (≤ 30 min, else `busy`); hold new task sessions on it on the home while the updater runs; run its channel's updater: npm `npm --prefix <p> install -g <pkg>@<v>`, Homebrew `brew upgrade --cask <token>`, an installer's own updater for the newest (`claude update`, `codex update`, `pi update --self`) or its pinned install for any other version (`claude install <v>`, Codex `install.sh --release <v>`); never an app's copy, Ducter's own pi, or an unknown copy. Judge by the version read back, never the exit code (updaters report success they didn't have). A copy that no longer answers `--version`, or whose login answered before and doesn't after, goes back to the old version where the channel pins (npm, Claude Code native, Codex standalone); a cask or pi's managed install can't, and the card says so. Steps **等它手上的事停好… / 在更新到 {v}… / 在检查 {v}… / 好了，现在是 {v} / 没更新成（，已经换回 {v}）** are `agent_update` events on the `devices` stream. (4) **Night** (D148's `autoUpdate` switch, off by default): in quiet hours, nothing working on it, one agent per look, only to a version inside the verified range: the channel's latest when verified, else, where the channel pins, the newest verified version; anything else waits for a tap. (5) **Workers** get the same `agent_update` op over their socket and send the fresh list of their agents (`agents`) after it. (6) **CLI** `ducter update --agents [--check] [--json] [--yes] [--all]`. (7) `scripts/probe-harnesses.ts` records each channel's latest beside the verified range. Rejected: one "latest" per agent from npm for every copy (a Homebrew or native user would be offered a version their updater can't install; casks lag npm by weeks, research/42 §5); auto-updating to any latest (the facts behind small windows and the partner's setup are checked per version, D135) | U (the author's goal), L, research/42 | `packages/protocol/src/{index,harness-facts}.ts`, `packages/core/src/{agents,harness-probe,devices,workers,core,ws}.ts`, `packages/runner/src/{runner,worker-host}.ts`, `packages/cli/src/{update,update-agents,worker,args,i18n}.ts`, `scripts/probe-harnesses.ts`, `apps/desktop`, `apps/web`, `design/system.md`, `design/harnesses.md`, `design/product-model.md`, `docs/devices.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `skills/ducter-{operate,deploy}`, `design/scenarios.md` (A7), `design/todo.md`, research/42 |
## 2026-11-10: Where a task runs (the author: "AI 涉及到选择不同的环境和 harness 这部分我们设计有了么，优雅高标准顺滑自然么？"; decided with "按建议，第一性原理把事情都做好，给用户最优雅体验和情绪价值")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D157 | **Decided 2026-11-10 (every proposed default taken). Where a task runs is part of who does it: one ranking over (computer × agent), picked from what the task needs, said in one quiet line, asked only when whose sign-ins act or "now vs wait" is at stake, and never widened without the person.** (1) **Needs, not names:** the partner passes what a task needs (a place; browse; browse as you, with the site when known; a Mac app; a pinned agent; long or ongoing; continuity) and core picks the computer; "在 MacBook 上做" stays a pin by name. (2) **One ranking:** `fw_candidates` takes every computer that runs tasks; per (computer, agent, model): hard filters (the needs, then the agent's own), then can-start-now over waits (asleep or can't be reached keeps its rows, ranked below), then your pin and rules (a rule may name a computer; a pin of an agent that lives on one computer pins that computer), then the least access that does the job (Ducter's own browser over the user's Chrome), then a computer that doesn't sleep for long work, then continuity (its worktree, session, or the user's uncommitted changes), then the agent's own rank, then the home. One reason, the step that set the pick apart from the best row on another computer (**一直醒着，合上 MacBook 也不停** · **要用你登录着的 {site}** · **只有 MacBook 有 Keynote**). (3) **When it asks:** never between equal computers; never when only one computer can (it waits, said once: **得用 MacBook 上的 Keynote，它醒了我就开始。**); one line with the default **等它醒** when the best computer sleeps and another could do it with a visible difference (other sign-ins, or the user must sign in there); always when the other computer would widen access; D128's line when the user's own pick can't run. (4) **Saying where** (*drawn in D161's coin language*): with one computer, never; with two or more, on every task, in the meta line (**在 hel 上** · **用你的 Chrome** / **用 Ducter 自己的浏览器** / **用 {app}**), the reason on hover or tap; this amends D152 (2)'s "when it isn't this machine". The conversation says where only when it waits or uses the user's Chrome. (5) **Changing it** (*the sheet's subtitle and group heads per D161 (6), (9)*): in words (a pin, restated; two moves the same way propose a rule); **换谁来做** opens one sheet for who and where: on the desktop, a strip of the Devices islands with each computer's coins (tap a coin = pick that agent there), then a list grouped by computer with one reason per row and greyed rows with why; a row on another computer says what moving does (**从最近保存的进度接着做；分支会先推到 {remote}。**, and **会用你的 Chrome，你登录着的网站它都能用。** when access widens); New task's Where chips gain a computer part only when the choice is real (a repo on two computers; No folder with two or more), opening **在哪台电脑上做**, and an agent that lives only on another computer appears in Who tagged **在 {device} 上**, picking it moves the computer part too. (6) **Moving (E3):** targets come from the same ranking (a folder, a Mac app or the user's Chrome can't move to a server, greyed with why); **我要合电脑了** or **合上之前搬走** is one decision for the computer, default move, naming what stays; long or ongoing work starts on a computer that doesn't sleep, so most closes need no move. (7) **Safety:** a worker never reads the conversation (D155 (3)); sign-ins never copy between computers; nothing moves or is picked toward more access without the user's tap, rule or Go; the user's Chrome only in a window of its own (D130 (4)); uncommitted work moves only through the branch. (8) **Motion:** no new visual concept; D81's parcel lands on its island at start, waits at the home end of the bridge while its computer sleeps, and moves home and out again (never island to island); reduced motion cross-fades. (9) **First build step:** browser places on a worker (`runner.ts:924`, D155 (3)'s roadmap item), since otherwise a Mac that does tasks for hel can't use the user's Chrome. (10) **The author's six calls (2026-11-10, all defaults):** (a) public pages with both computers awake run on the home's own browser (hel's, D151); the user's Chrome only when their sign-ins are needed; D130 still decides which browser *within* one computer. (b) The where line shows on every task once two or more computers run tasks. (c) **我要合电脑了** is one decision for the computer, default **move**, moving only what doesn't widen access. (d) New task: the computer is a part of the Where chip, shown only when there is a real choice (no fourth row). (e) Long or ongoing work prefers a computer that doesn't sleep, even when an awake laptop would start sooner. (f) 换谁来做 shows the islands strip on the desktop; the phone shows the grouped list only | U, L, R43 | `design/where.md`, `design/prototypes/where.html`, `design/product-model.md` (glossary, §3), `design/new-task.md`, `design/flows/EC-steering-places.md` (E3), `design/flows/A-setup-devices.md` (A3), `design/scenarios.md`, `design/todo.md`, `design/ui.md` ; built 2026-11-10: `design/where.md` §16, `design/system.md` "Placement", `docs/devices.md` |

## 2026-11-10: Notifications for the public iPhone app (the author: "你的 Ducter 还不能给这个 App 发通知：那台电脑上还没放 Apple 推送密钥", on the TestFlight app against a server home)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D159 | **The public iPhone app is notified through a small relay Nowledge runs, and the relay never sees what a notification says.** APNs takes a push only under the app publisher's key, which no user can or should hold (research/45), so D131's "each home sends to Apple with its own key" can't work for the TestFlight app. (1) **The relay** is one Vercel Node function next to the website, `https://ducter.ai/api/push/{register,send,revoke,health}` (`apps/site/api/push/[op].ts`; `node:http2` to Apple; no new provider). It holds the APNs key, a key of its own for handles, and an Upstash Redis store, all as Vercel environment settings (`design/release/push-relay.md`). (2) **End to end encrypted:** the app makes a 32-byte key (kept in a keychain group shared with its Notification Service Extension) and gives it to its home with the device token at subscribe time, over the paired, authenticated API. The home encrypts the title, text, where a tap goes and the decision id (AES-256-GCM, AAD `ducter-push-v1`, padded to 256-byte steps, keys redacted as in D152). Apple and the relay carry a neutral alert localized on the phone (`loc-key`: **Ducter 需要你看一下 / Ducter needs you**), `mutable-content: 1`, an allowlisted category and a collapse id that is an HMAC of the item under the phone's key. The extension (`DucterNotify`) puts the real words back and sets Go / Hold / Reply; if it can't, the neutral line shows and a tap opens the app. (3) **Abuse and state:** the app registers its device token with the relay itself and gets an opaque handle (the token encrypted under the relay's key, so the relay keeps no token database); the home only ever holds the handle. Limits: 30 sends an hour and 200 a day per handle, 600 calls an hour per caller address, 30 registrations an hour per address. The store holds revoked handle ids (400 days) and counters (an hour or a day), keyed by random ids and keyed hashes of addresses. A device's **断开 / Disconnect** (D155), turning notifications off, or connecting the app to another Ducter revokes its handle; connecting elsewhere also makes a new key. (4) **Home side:** a home with its own APNs key (`apns.json`, unchanged) sends straight to Apple, encrypted the same way, and falls back to the relay when Apple refuses that key (403); every other home uses the relay by default (`DUCTER_PUSH_RELAY`, `off` turns it off). `/api/me` says `apns`, `apnsVia` (`key` / `relay`) and `relay: "unreachable"` after a failed call; the phone says so plainly, and says when the app needs updating. (5) Web Push (D58) is unchanged: the no-app path. (6) The roadmap's "not planned: a hosted Ducter" holds: the relay forwards Apple notifications and nothing else. *Built in this change; not yet deployed: the relay's environment and the first signed build with the extension are the author's (`design/release/push-relay.md`).* | U (the author's report), L, research/45 | `apps/site/api/push/`, `packages/core/src/{push-relay,apns,web,core,devices}.ts`, `apps/ios/{DucterNotify,Shared}/`, `apps/ios/project.yml`, `apps/web/src/{push-client,views,i18n}.ts*`, `design/system.md` Clients, `design/product-model.md` glossary, `design/release/push-relay.md`, `design/release/ios.md`, `design/release/README.md`, `design/roadmap.md`, `design/todo.md`, `docs/phone.md`, `docs/privacy-and-safety.md` |
| D160 | **Updating is calm and honest: Restart Now never leaves a blank, frozen window, and "up to date" always says when it was checked.** Two bugs on the author's Mac (0.0.5 → 0.0.6). (1) **Restart Now** turned the window white with a beach ball for a while before the relaunch. Cause, measured on a scratch signed bundle: mygo closes the windows and stops the run loop in the same main-thread turn, so the close never reached the window server; the quit hook then re-checked the staged copy (`codesign --verify --deep`, team, `spctl`: 1.0–1.8 s there, first-time and longer on a large notarized copy) with the blank window still on screen. Now: after the password (if any), the window shows **正在换上新版本，马上回来 / Putting the new version in, back in a moment** (the working partner, ≥ 0.7 s) while `Updater.Begin` checks the copy and starts the swap off the main thread; then every window is ordered out and flushed, and the quit runs with nothing slow in it (7 ms measured). A copy that fails its check keeps the app open on the update card, which says why. Every quit flushes the window server right after closing the windows, so install-on-quit and a child Ducter's stop never show a frozen window either. The first launch after a swap says **已更新到 {v} / Updated to {v}** once, and doesn't restart the LaunchAgent the swap already restarted. (2) **"已经是最新的"** on hel's card was a 6 h old answer (0.0.4, with 0.0.5 and 0.0.6 out). Now the release is read every hour; the card says **已经是最新的 · {t}查过 / Up to date · checked {t}** with a quiet **现在检查 / Check now**; opening Devices or Updates and about reads again when the answer is older than 15 min; and a device, worker or app (its hello now carries `version`) on a version newer than the latest known makes the home read again at once (once per version per 15 min) | author's bug reports 2026-11-10; scratch-bundle timings (`.shots/update-ux/`) | `design/system.md` "Updating in place", `design/product-model.md`, `design/release/README.md`, `docs/install.md`, `docs/settings.md`, `apps/desktop/{lifecycle,main,flush_darwin}.go`, `apps/desktop/internal/update/update.go`, `packages/core/src/{release,updates,ws}.ts` |

## 2026-11-10: An update's outcome is judged by what runs (the author, Settings › 更新与关于 on 0.0.7: hel "0.0.7 · 没更新成", this Mac's worker "0.0.6 · 有新版本 0.0.7", and a lone "在查…")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D167 | **"Didn't update" is said only while the device still runs what it started from; the Mac's worker follows the app's updates; every state of a computer lives in its own row.** (1) **Root cause on the home (reproduced with fakes):** the restart helper writes `result.json` only after the restarted Ducter answered, but the home read it once, at its start, so it never saw its own outcome; the next update's Ducter read the previous one's (to 0.0.6) and, not running 0.0.6, called it a failure: 0.0.7 and 没更新成 at once. Any earlier failed attempt's file, an installer run or a slow start the helper gave up on did the same. **Now** the home reads the file again whenever it changes (15 min after its start, and on each card's view), a worker looks for it 10 min after it reached its main, and `judgeResult` decides against the running version: on the target → 回来了; still on `from` and not ok → 没更新成; moved on → nothing (marked reported). The card and both clients drop a failure the device has moved past (a home older than this rule). (2) **The health wait** is 180 s (was 60), the helper's journal says it's still waiting every 15 s, and readiness is told apart from the version: `alive.json` (a home writes it once it listens) counts as well as `/health` naming the version (a `/health` that doesn't say it, `DUCTER_LOCAL_TRUST=off`), an answer from another version is named in the reason, and a rollback that couldn't happen (no `ducter.prev`) is said instead of hidden. The helper is the previous binary, so (2) takes effect from the update after the one that brings it; (1) from the first start of a build that has it. (3) **This Mac's worker** (D155) kept running the old bundled helper from memory: the swap only kickstarted the home agent, and none at all when the app talks to a home elsewhere. Now the swap kickstarts `<bundle>.worker` too, and a minute after the app starts, a worker whose `alive.json` names an older version is restarted once per version (a plist naming another helper path is written again). (4) **Settings › 更新与关于 › 各台电脑上的 Ducter is built from shared pieces only** (`valueRow`, `sideStatus`, `sideLink`; a guard test fails on any `ui.*` laid out by hand there): 现在检查 and its 在查… sit at the home row's right where 已经是最新的 is; 没更新成 opens its why, what was seen, and 再试一次 under the row. The web's version block opens the why on a tap the same way, and its guard allows handlers only on shared controls. Copy: **devup.why.health** "新版本重启后三分钟里都没应答，所以换回了原来的。可以再试一次。" / "The new version didn't answer within three minutes of its restart, so the previous one runs again. You can try again." | U (the bug report), L | `packages/core/src/{update,updates,core}.ts`, `packages/cli/src/{update,worker}.ts`, `apps/desktop/{main.go,lifecycle.go}`, `apps/desktop/internal/{update/update.go,local/worker.go,store/store.go,views/{devupdate,settings,settings_update}.go,i18n/devupdate.go}`, `apps/web/src/{app,format,views,i18n}.ts*`, `design/system.md`, `docs/{install,troubleshooting}.md` |

## 2026-11-10: Nowledge Mem in Ducter's tasks (the author: "充分第一性原理，拉满思辨……OK 就直接做"; then "focus window harness 需要 Nowledge Mem 呀，我们团队工作重心在这里")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D168 | **(4) in part superseded by D393.** **A Ducter task runs with the user's own Nowledge Mem plugin, as the partner's identity; Ducter's own memory pieces only fill in where the plugin isn't, and the one switch holds.** Decided by the author ("focus window harness 需要 Nowledge Mem 呀，我们团队工作重心在这里"), replacing the draft that turned the plugin off. (1) **Mem on (the default when Mem is connected):** a task keeps the user's setup, the Nowledge Mem plugin included, and runs as the persona's identity: `NMEM_AGENT_ID` (and `NMEM_SPACE` when bound) per D141 (3), which the plugin's Context Bundle, searches and capture use (DOCUMENTED, the plugin's README: "for multi-agent orchestrators, set `NMEM_AGENT_ID` per spawned worker … keeping `source_app=claude-code`"). Its writes therefore carry the persona's identity and the agent's own `source_app` (claude-code, codex), not `ducter`: the plugin takes no extra provenance from the environment (VERIFIED by reading its hook scripts 2026-11-10: the env it reads is `NMEM_AGENT_ID`, `NMEM_SPACE`, `NMEM_HOST_AGENT_ID`, `NMEM_AGENT_CONTEXT`, the mailbox and config ones; its capture is `nmem t save --from <agent> --session-id <native id>`). The link back to the Log is that native session id, which the Log already keeps per task. (2) **Bridge stays with the partner:** a task also gets `NMEM_NO_MAILBOX_NOTICE=1` (DOCUMENTED), so messages to the persona's mailbox never surface inside a task; `NMEM_BRIDGE_SESSION_MAILBOX` is never set (D102's allowlist keeps it out). (3) **Mem off in Ducter (Settings › 记得什么, `DUCTER_MEMORY=off`), and only then:** the plugin is turned off by id in the task session (Claude Code `--settings {"enabledPlugins":{"nowledge-mem@nowledge-community":false}}` merged with the PreCompact settings; Codex `-c plugins.nowledge-mem@nowledge-community.enabled=false` when the user's `config.toml` has it) and no NMEM identity is set, so the switch is true inside tasks. This is the one exception to D17, and only when memory is off. (4) **Where the plugin isn't installed for that agent on that computer** (Mem's own check, D169), Ducter fills in: the few memories that match the title and brief in front of the first turn (`<what_i_know>`, ids, 6 s cap, logged by id) and a read-only task `memory_search` answered by the home (≤ 5 results, 6 per task, logged by query and ids; workers hold no Mem key). Where the plugin is there, neither: it already injects the Context Bundle at session start and after compaction and nudges a search on each prompt (VERIFIED in its `hooks.json`: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart, PreCompact, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionEnd), so a second recall would only double the context. (5) **Writing:** the plugin keeps the session's thread (its capture, under the persona); durable memories go one way: the task proposes `remember` (≤ 3) in its report, the partner keeps what is durable with `memory_add` and the task's provenance; the brief tells the task not to save or distill memories itself. Whether Mem distills captured threads into memories on its own, which could duplicate a `remember`, is not known (INFERRED risk; todo). (6) **Browser places get no memory** (the clean setup already leaves out every user plugin there, and the brief and the tool say nothing): the plugin injects the user's Context Bundle into the session unasked, and a page's text can steer the agent to type it into a form or a URL, a one-step leak with no search the agent chose to make; that is D62's reason, concretely. (7) Settings › 记得什么 says it: **…；替你做事时也用得上 / … and uses it in its tasks too**; off: **聊天和做事都不回想，也不记新的 / … in chat or in its tasks** | U (the author's direction), L (mechanics) | `design/memory.md` "Mem and tasks", `design/system.md`, `design/principles.md` (17), `design/product-model.md`, `packages/runner/src/{runner,brief,tools,oar}.ts`, `packages/partner/src/partner.ts` |
| D169 | **Nowledge Mem in the user's agents, per computer: Ducter shows where it is, recommends it where tasks would run without it, and installs it only by a task the user starts.** (1) **Check:** Mem's own `nmem --json plugins inspect` (local, read-only), on the home and on each worker through its `mem_plugins` op; at start, once a day, when a computer comes online, after a sign-in or an agent update (both refresh the devices), and when a setup task ends. A worker without the op, or without nmem, says nothing. The runner asks it whether a task there has the plugin (D168 (4)). (2) **One line per installed agent** in its coin detail (D161; the `coinLines` slot, its action in `coinActions`): **Nowledge Mem 已装 · 0.7.34 / Nowledge Mem 0.7.34 installed**; **Nowledge Mem 没装 / Nowledge Mem not installed** with **装上 / Install**; **Nowledge Mem 有新版 / … has an update** with **更新** (only when the check says so; today's check names no newer version); **Nowledge Mem 装了不止一份，要看一下** or **说不好 Nowledge Mem 装好没有，要看一下** with **理一下 / Sort it out**; **正在装 Nowledge Mem…** while its task runs; a computer that is away shows the line alone. "Installed" is never "working": every answer says runtime loading isn't verified, so that warning alone never turns installed into a review. (3) **装上 asks in place** (the card's own confirm block, shared controls only): **在 {device} 上给 {agent} 装上 Nowledge Mem？** and what it changes: **会在 {device} 上开一件事，照 Nowledge Mem 的官方说明来装：只改 {agent} 自己的设置，不动 Ducter。装好以后，重开 {agent} 才用得上。** Then one task on that computer, with that agent when it is signed in there (else any signed-in agent there), with the user's own setup, origin "you" (the tap is the Go): it follows https://mem.nowledge.co/SKILL.md for that host only, never guesses a URL or key and asks for a connect link when Mem isn't connected there, backs files up, verifies with `nmem --json plugins inspect --host <h>`, and says the agent must be restarted. The check runs again when the task ends. Never silent (D17). (2) **Architecture:** a broker connection (`connectors.md` §18); the broker gains MCP OAuth device sign-in (a link and a code the owner opens on their phone), tokens in `connection-tokens.json`; Tuwa's `tuwa-mcp.mjs` is never installed in a task. (3) **Who calls:** the partner only; a task that needs a call says so in its report and may read the result of the call it asked for. (4) **When to ask:** every call, with one Go / Hold card from Tuwa's own summary (who, what may be said, what stays private, voice, number, estimated minutes and cost), no countdown; GQ4's "don't ask next time" never applies; revisit after 3 approvals of the same number and goal in 14 days. (5) **Mid-call questions:** the top card with push, also in quiet hours, no default; after about 90 s unanswered the agent says it will call back. Settled 2026-11-11 (the author: "第一性原理做决定", defaults taken; built). User first: **who** is the heavy
multi-agent developer opening ten sessions across five repos in a morning, and, second, anyone who
wants "every weekday at 9" without a conversation. **Before:** a card of three rows of chips of
uneven height, a Start button of another family, nothing for later, and every start pulls them out
of where they were. **After:** words, one row, ⌘↩, next one; later and repeating work started the
same way and visible on On hand with when it runs. **First time:** ⌘N; the card's defaults are
right; the extra choices are pills that say their value (现在 / Now), shown, not explained.
