## 2026-11-16: the harness's own background work was invisible, nagged and killed (audit: a task's Claude Code `run_in_background` shell, Monitor or background subagent, or a Codex subagent, outlived its turn; Ducter nudged "Report status via report_to_main." at once, set the card to needs_you on the second miss, and parked the session after 15 min, killing the work with the process; Raft hit the same, research/05 §7)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D266 | **Built 2026-11-16 (runner, protocol, web, Mac) with fakes and OAR's scripted runtime; not yet seen on a live Claude Code or Codex task. A task's background work is the task working: Ducter counts it from the harness's own task events, shows its start and end as steps, keeps the session open and the card working while it runs, and asks for the report only after it ends.** *Who:* the developer whose task starts a 40-minute bench in the background and ends its turn ("I'll check back when it's done"); the consumer whose task waits on a long download; the fresh user, who only sees whether the task is at it or waiting for them. *Feel:* before, the card flipped to 等你 / needs you a minute after the task said it was running something, a nag landed in the task's turn, and 15 minutes later the work silently died; after, the task reads 在做, its transcript says **在后台跑着：{x}** and then **后台的事做完了：{x}**, and the report comes when the work is done. *How it starts:* nothing to learn: it is the same task, it just doesn't get interrupted. (1) **What OAR says (@botiverse/oar 0.95.1, read in `node_modules`):** `contracts/tasks.d.ts`: `task_started {taskId, taskType shell·agent·tool·workflow·other, description?, toolCallId?, background?, ambient?}`, `task_updated` (a patch: `status`, `background`, `description`), `task_ended {status completed·failed·stopped, summary?, outputFile?}`; `ambient` = work the runtime does for its own operation, to be left out. Claude (`runtimes/claude/tasks.js`) maps stream-json `system/task_started` (`is_backgrounded`, `ambient`), `task_updated` (`patch.is_backgrounded`), `task_progress` (a changed description) and `task_notification` (the end), from `local_bash`, `local_agent`, `remote_agent`, `mcp_task`, `local_workflow`; frames inside a subagent carry its `agentPath`. Codex (`runtimes/codex/tasks.js`) reports only its subagent threads (`subAgentActivity` started → `task_started` with `background: true` and the agent path as description; interacted → `task_updated running`; completed/interrupted → `task_ended`); **Codex's background terminals are not reported as tasks** in 0.95.1. OAR's stream-json driver follows a turn the runtime starts on its own (`shared/stream-json/session.js`, "spontaneous" turns: a `turn_active` with no input id), and its scripted runtime documents that "claude reports a background task's end whenever it comes" (`testing/scripted-tasks.d.ts`); that Claude Code starts a turn of its own when a background task ends is INFERRED (Claude Code's own behaviour, not exercised here). (2) **Counted:** the normalizer (`packages/runner/src/normalize.ts`) keeps the root's tasks (a subagent's own internals stay dropped, as before) and says one is in the background when it is flagged so, at its start or by a later patch, or is still running when the turn that started it ended (a foreground task always ends first, so an unflagged background one is caught too); ambient ones never. It emits a system line with `raw.background {id, act started·ended·stopped·failed, type, what}`; `HarnessSessionExt.backgroundLive()` counts them (`oar.ts`). The runner counts the same from the events (`TaskRt.bg`), so a worker's session, whose events cross the wire, needs no new frame. A new or ended session clears the count (its work went with the process). (3) **The nudge waits:** a turn that ends without a report while background work runs is neither nudged nor a miss; the card stays `working` and `hot`. When the last one ends between turns, the runner waits `backgroundSettleMs` (60 s) for the harness's own turn; that turn's end decides as any turn's does; without one, the one nudge goes, and a second miss leaves it to the user as before (the stall rule). (4) **Never closed under it:** `park()` re-arms instead of closing while background work runs (focus-window-states already said "no background work inside the window"; the code didn't look); the archive horizon skips such a task; the archive after a merge logs that it waits (`raw.archive: "waits_background"`) and archives when the last one ends, or at the next park. A drop, a stop, a move to another agent and quitting Ducter still close it: the person asked. (5) **A ceiling:** a background task the harness has said nothing more of for 12 h (`backgroundCeilingMs`, env `DUCTER_BACKGROUND_CEILING_MS`) stops counting, said once in the task (`raw.backgroundCeiling`); then it parks as any idle task. 12 h: longer than any bench or build the author runs, short enough that a forgotten `tail -f` costs one harness process for half a day, not forever. (6) **Shown:** a step kind `background` (`packages/protocol/src/steps.ts` `backgroundStep`, the Go port `apps/desktop/internal/views/steps.go`; both pass `fixtures/transcript.json`'s new case): act start · end · stop with its own description, a failed end an error row; words **在后台跑着：{x} / Running in the background: {x}**, **后台的事做完了：{x} / Finished in the background: {x}**, **后台的事停下了：{x} / Stopped in the background: {x}** (bare without {x}), label **后台 / In the background**, the waiting clock as its mark. A Codex subagent is said by its path's last part (`/root/explorer` → explorer). (7) **Not done:** Codex's background terminals (OAR does not report them; todo); a wait sentence on the card naming the background work (D261's "what it waits for") | The audit; OAR 0.95.1 source in `node_modules/@botiverse/oar/dist` (`contracts/tasks.d.ts`, `runtimes/claude/tasks.js`, `runtimes/codex/tasks.js`, `shared/stream-json/session.js`, `testing/scripted-tasks.d.ts`); research/05 §7 | `packages/runner/src/{normalize,oar,runner}.ts`, `packages/runner/test/background.test.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/{steps,transcript}.ts`, `packages/protocol/fixtures/transcript*.{ts,json}`, `apps/web/src/{i18n.ts,transcript.tsx}`, `apps/desktop/internal/{i18n/i18n.go,views/steps.go,views/transcript.go,views/tasksteps.go}`, `design/focus-window-states.md`, `design/product-model.md`, `design/todo.md` |

(4) **No empty openings:** output that says nothing ("Action completed.", "OK", "Done", empty) is dropped in the model, so such a step doesn't open. (5) **Errors as words:** a failed step stands on its own line in secondary ink with a small × and **出错 / Error**; under it one line in soft ink: the service's message unwrapped from its JSON, by its HTTP status ("GitHub 找不到这个文件（404） / GitHub couldn't find this file (404)"; 401/403, 429 and 5xx alike); a stack frame is never the telling line; the raw output only when opened. (c) **Ducter's own words are hairlines:** the person's phone lent or back, Ducter's browser handed back, a Stop, a reopen are sent with `from: "ducter"` (core's `tell`s and the runner's reopen, which went as from the user) and are a `told` block (`toldOf`; older lines from the user are known by their words): **你把 Pixel Fold 借给了它 · 19:07 / You lent it your Pixel Fold · 19:07**, **又能用了**, **你没把手机借给它**, **你让它停下了**, **你重新打开了这件事**, else **{name} 提醒了它一句 / {name} gave it a note**, what was sent on hover. (d) **Scroll that never fights:** cause (read, then shown by a test): the Mac re-pinned the page to its end every frame while the reader was within 4 pt of it, so a touchpad's first small steps were undone, and an opened run of steps was a 288-tall scroller of its own (the web's with `overscroll-behavior: contain`). Now the Mac's page is one `ui.List` (MyGo's virtual list) that follows its end only while the reader is at it, and an opened run grows in place (60 steps, then **还有 n 步 / n more steps**) on both clients; `TestTaskFirstWheelMoves` scrolls 3 pt at the bottom and checks the page moved on that first event and stayed. (e) **Fast on a long loop:** the Mac built every turn and remade the transcript each frame (69 ms a frame with 1,501 events in the test renderer); now the list builds only the turns near the view and the transcript is made once per change of the events (2.7 ms at the end with the working line's light, 0.4 ms mid-page). An opened task asks for its latest 2,000 events (from 500), so a day's loop is there; the 240-line "Show earlier steps" window is gone (the web skips settled turns off screen with `content-visibility`). (f) **The locator** (Mac and web, wide only): a rail at the transcript's right edge, one small rounded bar per turn, faint, the turns in view in ink; hovered or focused, a clay card lists the first line of what was said (the brief, your words, the partner's, each wake and note), newest at the bottom, those in view marked; a click goes there. Its name **这件事里说过的话 / What was said in this task**. (g) **Calmer words:** under the agent's words one quiet 11 line: **保存了进度** when saved (no flag), and on hover their time · how long the turn worked · **拷贝 / Copy**, drawn over the gap so nothing moves. *Defaults the author may revisit:* the locator's ticks evenly spaced by turn (not by height); wakes listed in the locator; a finished loop round still folds its findings when its last words are "45 分钟后再看" (todo). *Runner-up for (a):* keep the working line and change only its words, rejected because a card left on working by a progress report would still say 在做 with a clock running for hours | The author (2026-11-16) | `packages/protocol/src/{transcript,index,internal}.ts`, `packages/protocol/fixtures/transcript*`, `packages/core/src/{work,core}.ts`, `packages/runner/src/runner.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/{taskpage,taskturns,task,transcript,work,app,tasksteps}.go`, `apps/desktop/internal/i18n/loop.go`, `apps/web/src/{transcript.tsx,views.tsx,work.tsx,app.ts,i18n-transcript.ts}`, `apps/web/static/app.css`, `apps/web/demo.ts`, `design/{focus-window,ui,product-model,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/getting-started.md` |

## 2026-11-16: the partner in iMessage, through the Mac app (the author: chat apps as another window on the one conversation, D276; iMessage follows how the open-source gateways do it; research/88 §4, research/79 §3)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D277 | **Built 2026-11-16 (Mac app, protocol, home push) with fakes: a fixture `chat.db` in a temp directory and a fake sender; no real Messages database was read and no iMessage sent. iMessage is another window on the one conversation, carried by the Mac app, because only a Mac can read and send iMessage; the Mac app is a client of the home, so it works whichever computer the home is.** *Who:* the consumer personal-AI user first (an iPhone, Messages is where they talk, "my AI is a contact"), the heavy developer away from the desk; the fresh user meets one Settings card. *Felt:* before, another app to open; after, text the partner like a friend and it answers under its own name, never as them. *First time:* Settings › Notifications › **iMessage**: whose Apple ID, **连上 / Connect**, a six-digit code to text from the phone, the two permissions as rows. (1) **Mechanism, as the mature gateways settled:** read `~/Library/Messages/chat.db` read-only through the macOS `sqlite3` (spawned by the app, so the app's **Full Disk Access** counts; no cgo), by ROWID, polling every 2 s but querying only when the database or its WAL changed; decode `attributedBody` (typedstream, the first NSString, length-framed) when `text` is NULL; send with AppleScript through `osascript` (**Automation › Messages**), handle and words as arguments, never script text; pictures in from the attachment table as D206 media. No SIP-off helper, no hosted line, no Messages for Business. (2) **Identity, never as the person:** two labelled modes, **{name} 自己的 Apple ID（推荐）** (this Mac's Messages signed in to the partner's own Apple ID) and **给自己发信息 / Message yourself** (the person's own Apple ID: only the thread with themselves, every line starting **{name}：**). It sends only to the one linked handle, so it can't write to anyone else; in partner mode a sent message it didn't send means this is the person's Apple ID, and it stops and offers the switch. (3) **Pairing:** a one-time code made by the Mac app (10 min, one use); the first *received* message carrying it links its sender. Strangers get silence and nothing is kept; Settings says someone tried, at most once a day; group chats are never read. (4) **Routing:** the person's words go to the home as theirs (`send` with `via: "imessage"`, `clientId` `imessage:<guid>`; the home keeps `via` only from a desktop socket); every answer to a turn started there goes back (by `replyTo`); a turn started in an app is not mirrored; what Ducter starts itself goes there only when the person's last words came from iMessage and the Ducter window isn't in front, once, under the partner's quiet hours (findings dropped, the newest open card at the end of the night). (5) **Once:** the bridge tells the home `channel_status` (on, needs_permission, not_signed_in, error, off); while one says on and the last `user_msg` came via iMessage, the home's push stays quiet for decisions and done items (a live call's question still pushes). (6) **Decisions without buttons:** only the newest open card that is reversible and reaches no money, sign-in, key, phone, computer, person or agent, under 24 h old, is answered by a reply of 好 / 先等等 (and synonyms) or a Like / Dislike tapback on its own message; it says one line back; others say the question and **这件得在 Ducter 里定**; money, sign-ins, saved details and keys say only **有件事要你在 Ducter 里亲自定，这里不方便说。** Text out is flattened from Markdown, anything shaped like a key is replaced, long answers are cut at 1,800 characters. ## 2026-11-16: the author's phone-use run on a Pixel Fold: the person's turn to allow a recording, the loan's end said, a screen that stays on, tests that need the person

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |

| D280 | **Built 2026-11-16 (core, protocol, runner brief, web, Mac, Android app) with fakes; checked by tests (core through the real core with a fake phone, web and Mac words, the Android app's JVM tests and a debug build), not yet on the author's Pixel Fold.** *Who:* the author lending his own Pixel Fold for a long errand with a recording (a heavy developer), and the consumer who just wants "record it" to work and to get the phone back. *Feel:* before, Android's prompt to record sat on the phone unseen while he watched the Mac, and timed out ("no answer on the phone in 2 minutes"); the screen went dark during an idle loan; the task ended unsure whether the loan had ended ("借用是否结束还没确认"); after, every window says it is his turn and where to tap, the screen stays on, and the task and the page both say plainly when the phone came back. *First time:* nothing new to learn: a card like any of the person's turns, and a hairline. **(1) Android's recording prompt is the person's turn, said everywhere** (D248's "their hands are needed"): `phone_record_start` posts one card, **在 {phone} 上点「立即开始」，它才能录屏 / Tap Start now on {phone} so it can record the screen**, with **这是安卓自己的确认，只在手机上出现，只有你能点。录整个屏幕，不录声音。**, **还剩 {m:ss}** counting down Android's 2 minutes (`handset.until`), and one button, **不录了 / Skip recording** (no Go: only the phone answers it). It is a decision like any ask, so On hand lists it, the Mac notifies when its window isn't in front and phones get a push. It resolves by itself: the phone answers (**开始录了**, `go` by the user), the prompt gives up (**手机上没点，这次没录**, `hold` by default; the home gives up a little after the phone in case its word never comes), or the loan ends (moot). **不录了** sends `record_stop` with `skip`, which closes Android's dialog on the phone, and the task hears it once. On the phone the pill switches to **轮到你：点「立即开始」 / Your turn: tap Start now** over **安卓在问能不能录屏**, with the accent rim, the loan's notification the same; it is the task's again once answered. 「立即开始」 is the button the author's Pixel Fold showed; other Android versions word it differently (**共享屏幕**), so the card names the author's word, which a Pixel reader meets first (a per-phone word read from the dialog is later). **(2) The task always hears the loan ended:** every end is one line starting **Your loan of {phone} ended:** and saying the phone was returned (Stop, a lock, Android's switch, Remove; a loss keeps D255's words), and the phone tools answer the same words afterwards. The task finishing is never told (a message would wake a finished task) but logged as Ducter's own line (`from: "ducter"`), and a new task tool, `phone_give_back`, ends a loan the task no longer needs and answers once the phone let go. D271's `told` draws each as a hairline in the opened task: **你收回了 {phone} · {time} / You took back your {phone} · {time}** (`taken_back`), **它把 {phone} 还给你了 · {time} / It gave your {phone} back · {time}** (`given_back`), **{phone} 断开了，借用结束了 · {time} / Lost your {phone}; the loan ended · {time}** (`loan_lost`); the brief says the task always knows, so it never writes that it isn't sure. **(3) The screen stays on while lent; a timeout is not a lock.** Evidence [VERIFIED, AOSP `frameworks/base` main, read 2026-11-16: `services/core/java/com/android/server/wm/DisplayContent.java` (`applySurfaceChangesTransaction`, `mTmpHoldScreenWindow`, the per-display `SCREEN_BRIGHT_WAKE_LOCK` `mHoldScreenWakeLock`), `RootWindowContainer.java` (`handleNotObscuredLocked`), `WindowState.java` (`isDisplayed`, `isOnScreen`), `policy/WindowManagerPolicy.java` (`TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY` layer 31, above the keyguard 19 and the shade 17), `power/PowerManagerService.java` (`setWakeLockDisabledStateLocked`, `isAcquireCausesWakeupFlagAllowed`, `REQUIRE_TURN_SCREEN_ON_PERMISSION`), SystemUI `keyguard/KeyguardViewMediator.java` (`KEYGUARD_LOCK_AFTER_DELAY_DEFAULT = 5000`, `onStartedGoingToSleep`: `doKeyguardLaterLocked` for `OFF_BECAUSE_OF_TIMEOUT`, at once for the power key when `getPowerButtonInstantlyLocks` or not secure); DOCUMENTED: `WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON` "as long as this window is visible to the user", `PowerManager.SCREEN_BRIGHT_WAKE_LOCK` deprecated in API 17 "most applications should use FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON"]. So `FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON` *is* honoured for an accessibility overlay (no type check; `NOT_FOCUSABLE`/`NOT_TOUCHABLE` don't matter), but only while its window has a drawn surface that nothing full-screen and opaque covers, and it lapses with no sign when the pill isn't drawn [INFERRED: why it lapsed on the Pixel Fold isn't known; the emulator held it (D253)]. Chosen: keep the flag and add the app's own hold for exactly the loan's life, `SCREEN_BRIGHT_WAKE_LOCK | ON_AFTER_RELEASE` (deprecated *for apps with an activity in front*; an accessibility service has none; PowerManagerService still honours the level, it is the lock WindowManager takes for the flag, and refuses it only to a cached process, which a bound accessibility service with a foreground service never is; no `ACQUIRE_CAUSES_WAKEUP` on it; `WAKE_LOCK` is a normal permission; Google Play's wake-lock vitals count partial wake locks, and this one is visible, with the pill, only while the person lent the phone). Rejected: a periodic dummy gesture (it would touch the person's app and is a misuse of the accessibility API), an activity with `setTurnScreenOn`/`FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON` (it would take the front from the app the task works in), a partial wake lock (it keeps the CPU, never the screen). If the screen goes off anyway, the app reads the lock screen 1.5 s later: up, the person locked it, the loan ends (**locked**, as D253); not up, a timeout, the loan holds (`asleep` in its hello), nothing runs, the app turns the screen back on once (`ACQUIRE_CAUSES_WAKEUP`, `TURN_SCREEN_ON` declared) before Android's lock delay ends, and a task a tool told hears **…'s screen is on again** when it is; a second screen-off within 2 minutes of that wake is the person's. Limits, said: with *Lock after screen timeout: Immediately* a timeout still looks like a lock and ends the loan; with *Power button instantly locks* off the person's first press looks like a timeout once (the screen comes back) and the second ends it. The SCREEN_OFF broadcast no longer ends a loan by itself (the watch decides, within about 2.5 s). **(4) Tests that take the phone away need the person:** the brief's phone section and `phone_ask_user`'s description say never to lock the phone, turn on airplane mode, turn Wi-Fi off, swipe Ducter from recents or restart it yourself; ask the person with `phone_ask_user`, `what` the exact steps in their language, end the turn, then report what was seen (the message, `phone_look`, whether and how the loan ended), never what was expected. *Not built:* the per-phone word of Android's button read from its dialog; a human comprehension pass on the card and the hairlines | U (the author's run on a Pixel Fold, 2026-11-16, `todo.md`), AOSP source (above) | `packages/protocol/src/{handset,transcript}.ts`, `packages/core/src/handset/index.ts`, `packages/core/src/android/{tools,index}.ts`, `packages/core/src/{ws,core}.ts`, `packages/runner/src/brief.ts`, `apps/web/src/{handset.tsx,transcript.tsx,i18n-handset.ts,i18n-transcript.ts}`, `apps/desktop/internal/{views/{handset,components,liveview,taskpage,transcript}.go,i18n/{handset,loop}.go,protocol/handset.go}`, `apps/android` (`HandsetAwake.kt`, `Handset.kt`, `HandsetLife.kt`, `HandsetPill.kt`, `Recorder.kt`, strings, manifest, `HandsetLifeTest.kt`), `packages/core/test/handset-turns.test.ts`, `apps/web/test/handset-turns.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/handset_turns_test.go`, `design/{use-this-phone,product-model,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/phone.md` |

(3) **再找一次 / Look again always answers**: **正在找… / Looking…** for at least a moment, then **看过了 · 20:14 · MacBook 上还没看到手机 / Looked at 20:14 · no phone on MacBook yet** (or no adb there, found {phone}, waiting for Allow). An overlay over the in-call screen is not built. (7) **After:** 通话结束 / Done calling, then the partner asks how it went in one line and records it (D215's path). | # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D279 | **Built 2026-11-16 on the Mac and the web against the demo core's review loop (`t_loop`), for the author's review; LLM raters only (research/90). A task resting on a wait of its own says when it comes back, its look-now and stop buttons say their result, and the wait is drawn as a living clay ring with its looks counted.** *Who:* the developer with loops running all day (before: 在等 and 立即查看, which read as "open something for me to look at"; after: 21:59 回来, a ring filling toward 21:59, 看了 24 次), the consumer who asked it to keep an eye on something (wants to know it is not stuck and not needing them), the fresh user (nothing to learn: a time, a ring, two buttons that say what happens). *Felt:* 放心 (it is coming back, and when), 赏心悦目 and 惊喜 (the breathing bead, pebbles that collect, the ring closing with a tick when it comes true). *First time:* the first wait any task arms. (1) **The process** (research/90): six state candidates (在等, 盯着 / Watching, 守着 / On watch, 歇会儿 / Resting, **{time} 回来 / Back at {time}**, no state word), a mapping table each (盯着 and 守着 promise watching nonstop, false between looks and for timers, and 盯着 reads as surveillance; 歇会儿 reads as stopped; 回来 is false only for a task that won't come back on its own), a rubric, and Haiku raters one candidate per call in zh and en: all understood; 回来 least awkward (2.38, zh 2.25) and most alive in zh (4.0), Waiting most neutral in en; refined, "Back at 21:59" raised alive from 2.50 to 3.50 at the same comprehension. (2) **The state:** a blocked task with an armed wait of its own shows **{time} 回来 / Back at {time}** (another day: its day too; an event with no next look: **有动静就回来 / Back when it happens**) in the head's meta line (waiting ink, the clock mark), its On hand row (**21:59 回来 / back at 21:59** by the 12-pt ring, D261's **再看一次 / looks again** and **接着做 / goes on** retired) and the end line (**等 {what} · {time} 回来 / Waiting until {what} · back at {time}**, D271's **在等：… · 下次 …** retired). A task blocked without a wait of its own keeps **在等 / Waiting**; the On hand section stays **在等 / Waiting** (literal, true for all, first for en raters). (3) **The buttons:** **现在就去看一次 / Check now** (in zh a bare 看 reads as the person looking: 现在就看一眼 1/4 with no context, 现在就去看 0/4; 一次 makes it one round: 4/4) and **不用再去看了 / Stop checking** (3/4 zh, 4/4 en; 停止等待 2/4 zh, one rater read "deleted"), Check now first. (4) **The watch card** under the head: a 56 clay ring whose arc fills from the last look (or the arming) to the next, redrawn each half minute, a bead at its edge breathing once per 3.2 s (`--t-breathe`, Mac `Breathe`; still under reduced motion), how long is left inside; the rhythm (**每 45 分钟看一次**, an event **有新的就看一眼**, a timer **到点就接着做**) then the looks as pebbles (each wake in the transcript filled, each of the current wait's own looks hollow, at most 12) and **看了 24 次 · 上次 21:31** (**，还没有** when its own last look found nothing). The rhythm leads so a count never reads as watching nonstop (raters read "Looked 24 times" alone that way). A deadline keeps its groove inside the card. (5) **The moment it comes true:** for 2.6 s the card closes its ring in the done clay, pops on the spring (`--t-pop` 560 ms, Mac `Pop`), draws a tick and says **等到了，接着做 / Wait over, carrying on**; a task's own timer now counts as arrived too (both clients). (6) **Core:** a progress report while the task's own wait is armed leaves it on Waiting (`rests` in `decisions.ts`, from `work.waiters`), closing D271's todo: the card no longer flips to 在做 between rounds. *Defaults the author may revisit:* the section word 在等 kept; the tally counts wakes in the loaded transcript (its latest 2,000 events); Check now before Stop checking. *Alternative not taken:* 盯着 / Watching (warmest English, but it promises watching between looks and reads as surveillance in Chinese) | U (the author, 2026-11-16), research/90 | `packages/core/src/{decisions,core}.ts`, `packages/core/test/flow.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/{work.tsx,views.tsx,transcript.tsx,store.ts,i18n.ts,i18n-onhand.ts,i18n-transcript.ts,app.ts}`, `apps/web/static/{app.css,app.js}`, `apps/web/demo.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/{work.go,task.go,taskpage.go,waitcard_test.go,shell_shots_test.go,onhand_v2_test.go}`, `apps/desktop/internal/{i18n/{watch,loop,onhand,i18n}.go,theme/theme.go,protocol/protocol.go,store/store.go}`, `design/{product-model,on-hand,focus-window,ui,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/{waiting-and-routines,on-hand}.md`, `research/90-waiting.md` |

## 2026-11-16: a task is the person's own agent, and who does it changes inside the task (the author, moving his daily coding-agent work into Ducter: "单独 focus 的高度还原原版 harness 的原本能力和好的原始 system prompt / skill / tool"; "在同一个任务下切换 harness/model 等，不用新建 task session"; research/92)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D282 | **Built 2026-11-16 (runner, protocol, core, web, Mac) and checked by tests, and against the real Claude Code 2.1.325 and codex-cli 0.169.0 binaries with the model answered by a capture proxy (research/92); not yet on a real model, pi or DeepSeek Harness.** *Who:* the heavy developer who moves all of today's coding-agent work into Ducter and expects each task to be the Claude Code or Codex they run by hand, then wants Sonnet for the dull part and Codex for a second opinion without opening a new task; the consumer, who never sees a harness but gets the skills they installed; the fresh user, who sees a model and effort row and one quiet line. *Feel:* before, a task listed the person's 150 skills by name only, a Workflow they use daily was missing, and a model change meant a new session from saved progress; after, the same agent as by hand, a model or effort change that keeps every word of the session, and **换成 Codex 接着做 · 21:40** in the transcript. *First time:* 换谁来做 shows **模型 / Model** and **思考深度 / Effort** for the agent doing it; a tap is the switch. **(1) Fidelity, measured (research/92 §2).** Tasks already appended the brief (Claude Code `--append-system-prompt-file`, Codex `developerInstructions`) and kept the person's and the project's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md, hooks, subagents and MCP servers. Two losses, both from D135's small window: Claude Code sizes its skill listing at 1% of the window, so `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT` cut it from 40K to 8K chars and every skill and command arrived as a bare name; Codex sizes it at ~2% of `model_context_window`, which cut every description (13.8K of 18.0K chars). A task now sends `skillListingBudgetFraction: 0.05` in its `--settings` (the 1M window's 40K) and `-c skills.max_context_tokens=5440` (2% of Codex's default 272K window), giving the listing by hand, measured. The window and compaction point stay D135's. **(2) What a task leaves out, each re-justified (research/92 §3).** Kept denied: plan mode (approving a plan is the person's turn, a report_to_main with a default), ScheduleWakeup and Cron ×3 (a second clock that dies when the session parks; D267's `wait_for` time covers it, `/loop` included), AskUserQuestion (report_to_main asks), PushNotification and RemoteTrigger (around Ducter, outliving the task). **Workflow is allowed** in ordinary tasks: D241's reason for keeping Agent (the result returns to the task, which holds the brief) holds for a workflow's agents too; a browser place and the read-only partner still deny it. The brief stays appended, never replacing the harness's prompt; its content is only what Ducter alone knows. **(3) Slash commands in the task's composer.** Claude Code runs every one headless (measured: the person's commands and skills, `/review`, `/compact`, `/context`, `/cost`, `/clear`, `/model`), so they go to it as typed; `/model <name>` and `/effort <level>` are Ducter's on every agent (checked against the agent's own model list; a model or level it lacks is said as a failed line, nothing switches), so the card stays true; a bare `/compact` on Codex, whose app-server takes no slash commands, is OAR's manual compaction. **(4) Switching inside one task.** The same agent with another model or effort keeps its native session: the spec changes and the session reopens by its id with them before the next turn (at once when idle; after the running turn otherwise, so nothing the harness holds is lost): Claude Code `--resume <id> --model --effort`, Codex `thread/resume` with the model and the effort set on the loaded thread, OAR's documented same-runtime switch. Lossless. Another agent: the old session closes and is kept by agent; the new one starts with the brief (its instructions) and an automatic carry-over, condensed, from the task's own Log: the last six checkpoints, the last report and its questions with their defaults, the person's words since, the agent's last words, and what the branch holds; its tool calls, reasoning and compacted context are not carried. Switching back to an agent that worked on the task resumes **its own session** (in place, the same computer), told what happened since; this survives a restart (each `session started` line now names its agent; `raw.switched.back`). A move to another computer forgets them (the sessions stayed there). The task card, On hand, the Log and the transcript stay one task throughout. `task_switch` carries `effort`; core's switch for the same agent skips the candidate check and logs `body_selected` with the effort; the partner's rule hint still counts only changes of agent. **(5) Words.** The transcript draws each switch as one hairline with its time: **换成 {agent} 接着做 · {time} / Continued on {agent} · {time}** (`raw.switched`), **换成 {model} · {effort} · {time} / Now on {model} · {effort} · {time}** (`raw.retuned`), **换到 {computer} 接着做 · {time} / Continued on {computer} · {time}** (`raw.moved`); the in-place rows reuse New task's **模型 / Model** and **思考深度 / Effort** and say **换模型或思考深度，{agent} 还是接着这件事做，从下一轮开始。/ A new model or effort: {agent} carries on with this task from its next turn.**; the button to another agent stays **换到 X 接着做 / Continue on X**. *Not taken:* sending `/model` into a live Claude Code session (it works headless, but effort can't follow it, Codex has no equivalent, and the card would lie); a new task per agent (what the author asked not to have). *Open (todo):* pi and DeepSeek Harness on the same paths (resume by id with a new model is unverified there; a rejected resume falls back to the condensed start); a real-model run of a switch back; Codex `/compact` live. | U (the author, 2026-11-16), L (the calls), research/92 | `packages/runner/src/{oar.ts,runner.ts,brief.ts,browser.ts,index.ts}`, `packages/runner/test/{switch,task-tools,harnesses,runner}.test.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/{index,internal,transcript}.ts`, `packages/protocol/fixtures/transcript{-cases.ts,.json}`, `packages/core/src/{loadout,ws}.ts`, `packages/core/test/loadout.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/{views.tsx,app.ts,transcript.tsx,i18n.ts}`, `apps/web/static/{app.css,app.js}`, `apps/web/test/switch.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/{views/{loadout,transcript,taskturns,tasksteps}.go,views/switchtune_test.go,protocol/loadout.go,i18n/{i18n,loadout}.go}`, `design/{product-model,system,focus-window,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/{getting-started,settings}.md`, `research/92-native-fidelity.md` |

## 2026-11-16: the proactive bar (the author: "我希望你能好好打磨我们的 proactive ai，让它真的能像 grok bot / muse 那么好用、可靠、可信赖"; research/91)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D281 | **Built 2026-11-16 (core, protocol, web and Mac words) with fakes; checked by tests and a new life-days eval, not yet on the author's homes. What the person said comes back, the morning always comes once, and the morning says what Ducter holds for today.** *Who:* the heavy developer who says "下午 3 点提醒我…" between two task turns and has had the proactive side "send me nothing"; the consumer who expects Grok's or Muse's "it remembers what I said"; the fresh user with no account connected, for whom the conversation is the only source. *Feel:* before, a reminder lived only if the model armed a wait in that very turn, and a "好，明天提醒你" with nothing behind it was a broken promise in Ducter's own voice; after, 放心 (what it was told happens, at its minute, once) and 惊喜 (the morning starts with the thing they said yesterday). *First time:* nothing to set up: say it, and it comes back. **Evidence (research/91):** Pulse was retired (2026-06) for scheduled briefings called "faster, more reliable"; Meta's bots follow up once; help that was asked for carries none of the threat of help that wasn't (arXiv 2509.09309); the life-days eval (`packages/partner/eval/proactive/life.ts`, eleven scripted days through the whole engine on fakes) scored 0/8 before. **(1) 你说过的 / Something you said**, the eleventh find kind, read by code from the conversation (`proactive/said.ts`, no model): an ask to be reminded (提醒我… / remind me…), something the person said they'd do on a day (我明天要… / I need to … on Friday), and the partner's own promise to remind (only in answer to the person, within 10 minutes of their line: a reminder firing or a heads-up about tomorrow promises nothing). Never kept: a recurring ask (a routine's), a question, a guess or a state (要不要, 觉得, I'll be in…), the past, a forwarded message, a heads-up from the partner with no time. A wait the partner arms within 10 minutes of the line covers it (never two reminders); the partner's promise gives an undated ask its time. Said once at its moment: an exact time at that minute (its own timer); a day first in that day's morning note, outside the day's 3; an ask with no day the next morning; an ask for today said after the morning at 16:00 when an hour is left. An ask goes in every mode, 不用主动找我 too (they asked); a thing they'd do is proactive and never goes with it. Not said within 12 hours of its moment (the home was off), it is let go. Words: **提醒你：{what}。 / Reminder: {what}.** (with a time), **…{when}你让我提醒的。 / …You asked me {when}.**, **…{when}我说过会提醒你。 / …I said {when} I'd remind you.**, **你{when}说今天要{what}。 / {When} you said you'd {what} today.**; How I know is their own line, **你说的：「…」 / You said: "…"**, never anything else. Asked items push time-sensitive, the rest passive; 这类不用告诉我 mutes only what they said they'd do. "Anything for me?" (`noticed`) lists the ones still ahead first. **(2) The morning always comes once:** a home that was not running or awake at the end of quiet hours (a restart, a night update, a Mac asleep at 08:00) makes the note at its next tick, up to 4 hours late (`MORNING_LATE_MS`); later, the day is skipped rather than a "morning" note in the afternoon; a home that never had a morning starts with tomorrow's. **(3) The morning's one line**, after the greeting and only when it holds something: the reminders the partner set for today (**今天 {time}：{reason}。 / At {time} today: {reason}.**) and cards waiting on the person for over 12 hours (**还有 {n} 件等你定，最早的是{when}的。 / {n} things are waiting on you, the oldest since {when}.**, each card named once, never again). A day with only this line sends the note, passive; a day with nothing still sends nothing (D173 stands). What finished overnight is not repeated: the partner said each outcome when it happened (D104's 你不在的时候 marks the gap). **Numbers (fakes only):** life.ts recall 0/8 → 8/8 in window, precision 7/7, 0 late, wording 7/7; run.ts 7/7 and the dots day 7/7 unchanged; 23 ordinary lines never kept (tuned on that corpus, not held out). Tradeoff: rules miss phrasings a model would catch (a miss is silent, as before; a wrong keep is one line the person can mute); the alternative, a cheap model over every turn, costs a call per message and reads the conversation for Ducter's own sake. The persona is unchanged; one partner tool (the notice rule's list of kinds) gained `said`, so D175's run: Haiku 76/112 (`2026-11-16-haiku-d281.md`; 84/112 on 11-13 over fewer scenarios; the proactive ones fail as before, and `timer-set-en` failing with "no reminder set" in both runs is gap (1) seen in the model). *Not built (`todo.md`):* the live week on the author's homes, a held-out set from real conversation, a model pass for missed phrasings, the language pinned when unset, a trust number per kind, "done" for a kept line | U (the author, 2026-11-16), research/91 | `packages/protocol/src/proactive.ts`, `packages/core/src/proactive/{said,engine,words}.ts`, `packages/core/test/{proactive-said,proactive-own}.test.ts`, `packages/partner/eval/proactive/life.ts`, `apps/web/src/i18n.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/i18n/accounts.go`, `design/{connectors,product-model,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/waiting-and-routines.md` |

## 2026-11-16: On hand with character: the partner at its head, the work as cards, the day beside it (the author, after D270: "我总觉得这里的设计不够好，有点乱，缺乏细致打磨，缺乏让人非常欢呼的好，那才是我们的标准，现在显得平庸而且不够有追求和有性格，不能拉满给用户的情绪价值和 beloved 的水平"; their screenshot: 现在没有要你定的事。, the strip 0 · 0 · 4 · 1, flat rows under 在等 4, two folds, an empty canvas)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D287 | **Built 2026-11-16 on the Mac and the web against the demo core's moments (`apps/web/demo-onhand.ts` `DEMO_STATE` author, quiet, one, busy, waiting, the long day, a fresh few), for the author's review; LLM raters only (research/95). On hand's board has the partner at its head, its pose saying how the whole stands and one sentence of facts in its voice; what is alive stands as small clay cards with the agent's coin and a truthful heartbeat; a wide window has the day beside the board; a fold earns its line from three.** *Who:* the developer opening it dozens of times a day (wants the whole in one sentence, then the one card to look at, and a sense of a team at work); the consumer (wants 放心: someone minds it and says when it's back, and never "在等" read as "waiting on me"); the fresh user (sees the partner and its one or two errands as cards, nothing to learn). *Felt:* before, a plain list that looked the same at 4 or 40 with a void under it; after, the partner on its bench says **现在没有要你定的。4 件在等：最早 22:40 回来，2 件一天多没有动静；今天做完 1 件。**, its errands stand as cards with their rings filling toward when they come back, and the day column says what's next and what came back today with its result. 赏心悦目 (the clay figure and coins, cards that lift under the pointer), 放心 (every number and time is the Log's), 惊喜 (a new result's card pops once and glows), 好用 and 顺滑 (the same keys, filters and folds). *First time:* zero setup. (1) **The process** (research/95): seven candidates (the literal list, the partner with its cards, a day timeline, a clay village, a garden, four columns, the partner's note), a mapping table each with false implications (village and garden: a dark house or a wilted plant reads as broken or neglected, and need new art; the timeline hides titles; the note needs a model per open), a rubric, Haiku raters (3 personas × zh/en): the list calmest but least alive (2.17) and least delightful (2.50); the partner with its cards most delightful (4.00); refined from its misreadings it held legibility (3.83) and passed the list on scale (3.67). (2) **The head:** the partner's own clay figure (76 on the Mac and the web's whole screen, 56 in the side pane and on the phone) in the pose for the whole, never per task: its flag when anything needs you, reading while anything works, on its bench while everything waits, smiling when all that is left came back done today, idle otherwise; it breathes and blinks as the avatar does (still under reduced motion). Beside it **one sentence, always**, from counts and times only (never a model, D261 (9)): **现在没有要你定的。/ Nothing needs you.** or **有 n 件要你定。/ n things need you.**, then **n 件在做 / n at work**; **n 件在等：最早 {time} 回来，m 件一天多没有动静 / n waiting: the first back at {time}, m quiet for over a day**; **今天做完 n 件 / n done today** (18/600 in the display face, balanced lines). It replaces D261 (4)'s calm sentence that showed only when nothing needed you. The strip stays under it as the filters. (3) **Cards for what is alive:** working tasks, fresh waits and new results stand as small clay cards (white on a 2-pt ledge, radius 20, two to a row from 612 of list width, one on a phone), each: the agent's coin at 28 (D183, D213; it rocks while working, bobs while it waits on you), the title 15/600, what it is on in two lines (the row's sources, D261 (5)), and at its foot the **heartbeat**, always true: working, three soft bars rising and falling in the working blue and **在做 12 分钟 / at work for 12 min** (**刚开始做 / just started** under a minute); a wait, the 16-pt ring of D279 filling toward **22:40 回来**; a finished one, **14:10 做完 / done at 14:10**; on the right +a −d, 草稿 PR / 已合并 and where. Working cards carry a faint blue wash at the top, a new result a green wash and glow with its result in full ink and the smiling face; the first time a new result's card is drawn this session it pops once on the spring (`--t-pop`). Hover lifts a card 2 pt (none under reduced motion) and offers its one next step (Merge, Draft PR, Pause); the card under the keys has the accent outline. Quiet waits and seen results stay rows, and the rail beside an opened task stays rows (D244). The D261 groove is not on a card (its ring is the heartbeat; the groove is in the opened task's watch card). (4) **The day beside the board** (Mac ≥ 1280 pt, web ≥ 1280 px): a thin line of time, **接下来 / Next** (the waits' next looks and defaults taking effect, soonest first, at most 5, hollow beads in the waiting ink), **{time} 现在 / Now** (the accent bead, breathing on the web), **今天回来的 / Back today** (today's finished tasks, newest first, at most 6, each with its result's first line, filled done beads); each opens its task. Where it shows, D127's one-line forecast is not drawn (the column says it). The beads mark times on a line, not a task's state (D69's "a face, never a dot" is about state). ## 2026-11-16: an opened task opens at once, its locator glides, and Ducter's own lines stop reading as the person's (the author, the Mac app against a remote home on a VPS: "打开一个任务要转圈差不多十秒", "点定位栏直接跳过去，没有动画", "Ducter 自己发给它的指令还是显示成我的橙色气泡")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D284 | **Built 2026-11-16 on the Mac (test renderer) and the web, for the author's review.** *Who:* the developer with long loops on a server home (before: 正在加载… under the head for about ten seconds, then a jump with no motion, and their transcript full of orange bubbles they never wrote; after: the page is there at once, a click glides, only their words are theirs), the consumer opening a task from their phone over the home's tunnel, the fresh user (nothing to learn: it opens, it moves, what they pressed reads as a press). *Felt:* 顺滑 and 放心 (it opens like a chat app; nothing is said in their voice that they didn't say). *First time:* opening any long task on a remote home. (1) **Why it took ten seconds, measured** (a 5,000-event review loop, its newest 2,000 asked as D271 did; the Go and web perf tests): the home's read was 6.5 ms (indexed on (stream, seq)); the frame was **3.86 MB** of JSON, mostly tool output previews, sent uncompressed on the one socket: **8.0 s** over a 4 Mbit/s link with an 80 ms round trip; then the Mac decoded it and made the transcript on the UI thread in **1.2 s** (its key redaction ran nine regexps over every 2 KB output: 1 s of it). Before the last byte nothing of the transcript showed: **9.2 s to first paint**. (2) **Newest first:** an opened task asks for its newest window (**200 events**) and paints it the moment it lands; older pages (**300 events** each, `beforeSeq` the oldest it holds) follow one at a time in the background up to **2,000** (D271's reach), then only as the reader scrolls up to the head, with no limit. The home answers each page with `more` (older ones remain) and echoes `beforeSeq`; a home before D284 is read as "a full page may have more" (at worst one more page comes back empty). (3) **Cached per task:** what the client holds shows at once when the task opens again, and nothing is asked; a new socket marks every loaded task stale (live events reach only a socket that is up), and its next open asks the newest window again, which keeps the cache whole when it meets what was held. (4) **Gzipped when asked:** a client that says `hello.gzip` (the Mac app; the web where the page can unzip) gets a frame over 16 KB as one binary message, its JSON gzipped (tool output compresses several times over: the window's **369 KB is 104 KB**). (5) **The Mac's transcript is made faster:** key redaction runs a pattern only where the text holds what it needs and keeps its answers for long texts; a task event's body is decoded once; 2,000 events now take **~120 ms**, a window **~60 ms**. **After: 104 KB, 0.30 s on the same link, painted 62 ms after it arrives (0.36 s to first paint); the web's window is ready 23 ms after it arrives.** (6) **The locator moves calmly:** a click eases to the turn (the Mac row by row on an ease-in-out curve over 260–520 ms by distance, a near turn gliding pixel by pixel; the web an eased glide of 280–640 ms that lands a screen short first when the turn is more than three screens away), at once under reduced motion; the turn then wears a soft clay tint (the accent at 14–16%) that rises fast and fades over 1.6 s; the turns in view sit on a clay thumb on the rail that glides as the page moves; the hover card rises out of the rail (scale 0.94 → 1 and fade from its bottom right, 180–200 ms; back into it on leave, 120 ms; a plain fade under reduced motion). (7) **Ducter's own lines, at the source:** an answer on a card is relayed from **"ducter"** (core's `forwardFrom`: a Go, a key given or refused), only a reply is the person's own words ("user"), on the live path and on the re-send after a restart; the phone, computer and browser notes already were (D271, D280). (8) **In the model (both ports, `goRelay`, `toldOf`):** a Go relayed (**User says Go: {label}.**, and core's longer relays: **The user says they're done on the phone (…)** as Done, a sign-in, a payment, a tunnel, a saved thing's use as the plain Go) is a new block, **go**, that opens a turn and is drawn as a quiet chip on the person's side: **你点了「好，Done」 · 20:14 / You chose “Done” · 20:14**, what was sent on hover, never an orange bubble; Ducter's words logged as the person's before D271/D280 are hairlines: **The user stopped you using their phone** as **你让它停下了 / You stopped it**, a recording's answer or the phone's screen waking as **{name} 提醒了它一句**, and any other user-role line that begins **The user** the same (a person never calls themself "the user" to their agent). (9) **The locator lists only what was said:** the brief, the person's words and the partner's, each in ink; between them each run of quiet turns (a wake, Ducter's note, a Go relayed) is one muted line: its own words for one, **等到了 {n} 次 · {from}–{to}** for wakes only, **{n} 条提示 · {from}–{to} / {n} notes · {from}–{to}** for a mix; on the rail a quiet turn is a short tick. *Defaults the author may revisit:* the window of 200 and pages of 300; **{n} 条提示 / {n} notes** for a mixed run; the chip's words **你点了「…」 / You chose “…”**; the web gzip needs the browser's DecompressionStream (Safari 16.4+), else it takes text as before. *Alternative not taken:* the socket's own deflate (permessage-deflate): the Mac's WebSocket library has none, and turning it on for every socket changes the phone app's and the workers' links too | U (the author, 2026-11-16) | `packages/core/src/{ws,core,decisions}.ts`, `packages/core/test/{server,flow}.test.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/{index,transcript}.ts`, `packages/protocol/fixtures/{transcript-cases.ts,transcript.json,longtask.ts}`, `packages/partner/eval/run.ts`, `apps/web/src/{app,store,conn,views,transcript,i18n-transcript}.ts(x)`, `apps/web/static/app.css`, `apps/web/test/task-open.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/{client/client.go,protocol/protocol.go,store/store.go,redact/redact.go,i18n/loop.go}`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/{app,taskhistory,taskpage,taskturns,tasksteps,transcript}.go` and their tests, `design/{product-model,ui,scenarios,todo}.md` |

*Note, 2026-11-19 (D284 (5), no new decision):* on a loaded Mac TestTaskOpensFast failed now and then on 0.0.88 and on 0.0.89 alike (one page over 300 ms). pprof: half the paint was building the turns of a page that had just landed; each turn is built once (the cache already keeps the rest), and two thirds of that was key redaction's secret-named-field pattern, which ran unanchored over every 2 KB output. It now runs only where a secret's name begins (Go `fieldMatches`, TS `replaceField`), with the same output: the old pattern is the oracle in `field_test.go` and `redact-field.test.ts` over 300,000 and 200,000 generated texts, and `fixtures/redact.json` gains the prefix forms (`config.api_key`, `x-api-token`, `MY_SECRET_KEY=`, mixed case, across lines). The field step on a 30-line output: Go 1.16 ms to 0.14 ms, TS about 140 µs to 35 µs; in the no-index test redaction went from 0.98 s to 0.39 s of CPU, building from 1.25 s to 0.63 s. TestTaskOpensFast now answers task_index as core does and measures the real path (first paint 51–204 ms after the window lands, 5 of 5 runs passing); the no-index path is TestTaskOpensFastNoIndex. TestLongSessionWindowed's scroll p95 at 50,000 events: 44–131 ms before, 30–66 ms after; its 50,000-event jump, over budget in 4 of 5 runs before, passed in all 5 after.

Each fact is its own element with its own role: (1) **a name is the title alone**, never with a kind or brand appended; (2) **one secondary line only when it reads as a natural phrase** in the partner's voice ("14 小时前在线 / Online 14 hours ago", "在 hel 上跑"); (3) **a state is a state word in its ink with its dot**; (4) **counts and times are their own muted elements**, tabular, right-aligned in a row; (5) **a kind is the icon or the art**; (6) **a group of metadata is separate small elements spaced by a gap token** (`facts` on the Mac, `Facts` on the web, S3, free to wrap); (7) **provenance is a quiet chip or label**; (8) **plain text (a push, a notification, a toast, copied or shared words) is one natural sentence**; (9) **an accessible name reads the facts aloud** (`spoken`: "，" / ", "). Allowed, as typography: an en dash in a range (23:03–23:04). The platform says the app (`ios-app`, `android-app`) or the browser (`ios-safari`). A second one of a model is "iPhone 2". ## 2026-11-17: Bridge after Mem's sender fix (Weizhen: "这里的部署已经好了"; "local 版本需要带上一些 bugfix，就可以使用了"; research/66 §8)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D294 | **Built 2026-11-17 with fakes only; the live rerun did not run. Ducter reads Mem's new sender and reply fields the day a CLI carries them, never offers an agent Mem can't deliver to, and treats Mem's "can't right now" as a short wait, never as a reason to send twice.** *Who:* the author's own terminal agents (Claude Code, Codex) writing to the partner, and the partner asking them for the author. *Found (2026-11-17):* Mem Cloud runs #10278, but it is a representation the CLI asks for and nmem 0.10.119 (the newest, 11-14) predates it: a re-opened reply still has no `sender` and no `in_reply_to`; the trial's preflight stops at a second active `ducter` connection (hel, D258); the Mac's Mem app runs in Cloud mode, so a local Bridge can't be tried there. (1) **Sender.** `sender.agent` names the agent; Mem's generic "Bridge agent" (every native session) counts as unnamed (一个 AI agent, D273). In the user's "Only me" place every sender is theirs whatever `sender.member` says; elsewhere only a member equal to the user's own. `in_reply_to` links an answer to Ducter's message (follow-through then stops by itself). (2) **Contacts.** A card with `mailbox_available: false` is left out (the 2026-11-13 409 can't recur). (3) **Transient refusals.** 503/429, `_busy`/`_unavailable`/`_capacity` or `retryable: true`: reads retry after 0.4 s and 1.2 s; a send or reply only when Mem says it was not admitted (`outcome_unknown: false`). Still busy: failed, not sent, and one line in the partner's voice: **你让我发的消息没发给 {agent}：Nowledge Mem 那边这会儿收不了，不是你这边的问题。这次什么都没发出去，过一会儿再跟我说一声，我重新发。 / I couldn't send the message you asked me to send to {agent}: Nowledge Mem can't take messages right now, nothing wrong on your side. Nothing went out; tell me again in a little while and I'll send it.** (4) **Mem's word on the outcome first:** `outcome_unknown: true` is never called refused; `false` with a registered code is refused, not unknown. (5) **No " · " joins (D291):** **{agent} 发来请求：「{gist}」 / Request from {agent}: "{gist}"**; a teammate's agent **{agent} ({team})**. (6) The trial's S2 card check follows D273 (the agent by its own name); its preflight says whether nmem carries the new fields. *Tradeoff:* up to 1.6 s more before a busy send is called failed; the alternative, queueing a busy send and sending it later by itself, saves a retap but sends something the user may no longer want. *Upstream:* five drafts for Mem in research/66 §8.4 (not posted) | the author's brief (2026-11-17), research/66 §8 | `packages/partner/src/{bridge.ts,bridge-out.ts,partner.ts}`, `packages/partner/eval/{fake-bridge-nmem.ts,bridge-live.ts}`, `packages/partner/test/{bridge-presentation.test.ts,bridge-out.test.ts}`, `apps/web/src/i18n.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/i18n/i18n.go`, `design/{bridge,product-model,roadmap,todo}.md`, `design/prototypes/bridge-asks.html`, `research/66-bridge-released.md` |

## 2026-11-16: any language, not Chinese or else English (issue #5; the author: "我们不能假设除了中文就是英文", research/99)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D292 | **Built 2026-11-16 (protocol, partner, runner, core, CLI, the web client, the Mac app) and checked by tests and the partner eval with haiku; no real Korean user's home was used.** Three different things get three tags. (1) **The conversation language**: what the person writes in, any language, a BCP 47 tag. Detected per message by Unicode script first (Hangul → ko, kana → ja, Han → zh, or zh-Hant when Traditional-only characters lead), then a small stopword and diacritic score inside Latin, Cyrillic and Arabic; code, links, paths and numbers are not language. A message with none of its own (OK, a number, an emoji, a command, a code block) keeps the last known one; an unsure one keeps it within its script, and unsure Latin never moves it off another script. It is folded from the Log's user messages, so a restart reads the same (`packages/protocol/src/lang.ts`, the Go twin `apps/desktop/internal/lang`, one fixture file). (2) **The report language**: the partner carries the conversation language (or the fixed setting) as a tag to the task (`language` on `task_open`, any tag; "zh" and "en" still read), its brief names it ("Language: Korean (한국어)"), D154's hold-back and the card check use `inLanguage` (by script where scripts tell; a Latin language is held back only when its words clearly say another known Latin language; an unknown one is let through), and every client checks and shows a task's report against **that task's language**, then the conversation's, never the interface's alone. (3) **The interface locale**: a tag resolved to a table through a fallback chain (zh-TW → zh-Hant → zh → en; ko → en); `negotiate` picks the first preferred language that has a table; plurals by CLDR category (`key.one` / `key.other`), numbers and dates by Intl; `{name}` placeholders, not concatenation. Only zh and en have tables and only they are offered; the engine doesn't care. (4) **The partner** names the language of every user message by name and autonym (`[language] The user wrote this in Korean (한국어): reply in Korean (한국어), including the first line.`), Chinese included (before, Chinese got none and everything else got "English"); a message with no language gets the conversation's; a report turn names the conversation's. The persona says "whatever it is". (5) **回你用的语言 / Replies in** takes any language: **跟着我 / Follow me**, the common ones by their own names (简体中文, 繁體中文, English, 日本語, 한국어, Español, Français, Deutsch, Português, Italiano, Русский, العربية), and **其他语言… / Other language…** for the rest of `languages.json`. (6) Lines the code writes itself (an ack the model didn't write, a card Ducter builds, words to another agent) come from zh and en tables through the chain: English for a language without a table, which is honest and the next thing to improve (a table, not a branch). Before any language is known they stay Chinese as before (`NO_WORDS_YET`). (7) Message bubbles carry `dir="auto"`, so Arabic and Hebrew read right to left. (8) A guard (`packages/protocol/test/lang-guard.test.ts`) fails on a new inline zh/en branch; its allowlist is a ceiling that only shrinks (research/99 §7 lists what is left and why). | issue #5; research/99 | `packages/protocol/src/lang.ts`, `languages.json`, `say.ts`; `packages/partner/src/partner.ts`, `persona.ts`, `bridge-out.ts`, `words.ts`; `packages/runner/src/brief.ts`; `apps/web/src/i18n.ts`, `app.ts`, `views.tsx`; `apps/desktop/internal/lang`, `i18n`, `say`, `views/partner.go`; `design/system.md`, `conversation.md`, `ui.md`, `product-model.md`; `docs/settings.md` |

## 2026-11-17: how the machines reach each other: liveness, the home's key and its addresses, and Devices says how (research/97 steps 1–3)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D293 | **Built 2026-11-17 (protocol, core, runner, CLI and workers, web, Mac, iPhone, Android): research/97's first three steps. Checked by tests with fake clocks, fake sockets and fake homes, and in shots against a demo core (`.shots/d293/`); not yet on a real tailnet, a real Cloudflare account, a real second network or a Mac that really sleeps.** *Who:* the heavy developer most (a server in a tailnet, a MacBook doing tasks for it, a phone that is sometimes in the tailnet and sometimes not); the consumer with a Mac at home and a Cloudflare tunnel; the fresh user never sees a network word. *Feel:* before, a laptop that changed Wi-Fi left a dead socket for up to two minutes and then lost its running sessions; a home had one address, chosen by whichever command ran last, and switching meant pairing every device again; nobody could see which way a device was connected or that a tunnel lets Cloudflare read the traffic. After, a blip is a calm "reconnecting" and the same session carries on, a home keeps every way to reach it, every native device picks the best way that proves it is the home, and Devices says plainly how each device is connected. *First time:* nothing new to do: the next welcome carries the ways, and the card shows them. **(1) Liveness.** Every socket on the home is pinged (a WebSocket ping every client answers by itself) every 15 s and cut after 45 s of silence (`core/src/workers.ts` `createLiveness`, one sweep for client and worker sockets). A worker pings every 15 s and redials after 45 s without an answer, and at once when its ping timer fires more than 10 s late (the computer slept) (`cli/src/uplink.ts` `createPinger`). A client pings only a home whose welcome says `ping: true` (the web every 15 s, also skipping one interval when the browser paused the page; the Mac app with a 45 s read deadline), so a 0.0.60 home is never closed for silence. The Mac app says `{t:"sleep"}` on its own socket at system sleep and dials nothing until it wakes, then at once (`client.Sleep`, `Wake`, mygo's power events); the home marks the worker on that Mac's computer asleep too, so its tasks read 睡着了 / Asleep at once (the worker process can't hear the system's sleep itself). **(2) A worker's sessions survive a drop.** The worker keeps one host for the life of its process; after a drop it holds its sessions for 2 min and keeps what they say (at most 5000 frames, else the grace ends early); its hello after the drop names the sessions it still holds (`held`); the home holds them 2 min 15 s, ends the ones not named and reattaches the rest, and the buffered frames flush in order after the welcome. A worker from before D293 names none, so its sessions end as before. In the task: the residency is offline and work in flight says **正在重新连上 {device}… / Reconnecting to {device}…**; back in time: **{device} 连回来了，接着做 / {device} is back; carrying on**, the same session, nothing resumed; past the grace the old path (resume by id), and the wait before **在等 · {device} 连不上** counts from the drop, not from the end of the grace. Never failed, never blocked during the grace. **(3) The home's key.** Ed25519, made at first start in `<dataDir>/home-key.pem` (0600, beside `devices.db`), never printed; the fingerprint (SHA-256 of the raw key, first 16 bytes, base64url, 22 characters) rides in pairing links (`/pair#c=<code>&k=<fp>`: the code is still read by every older parser), in the pairing answer (`fp`, `key`, `ways`), the welcome (`fp`) and the ways frame. `GET /.well-known/ducter-home?n=<nonce>` answers before the gate (a device asks a way before it shows that way its token) with the key and its signature of `ducter-home\n<nonce>`; a device accepts a way only when the key's fingerprint is the one it pinned (the link's `k`, else the pairing answer, else, for a device paired before D293, the first welcome over the token it already had). **(4) The address book.** `<dataDir>/reach.json` (0600, no secrets): ways `{kind: lan | tailnet | domain | tunnel, url}`. `ducter domain`, `ducter tailscale` and the Cloudflare tunnel each add or take out their own way and never overwrite another; `public-url` stays as the primary, the address pairing links lead with and the only one an older client knows: the first way added is the primary, a later one leaves it alone, and when the primary goes the next that reaches the most devices takes it (domain, tunnel, tailnet). A `public-url` from before D293 is a way too and joins the book when another is added. The tunnel no longer refuses to start beside a domain in the book; only an address set by hand (`DUCTER_PUBLIC_URL`) still counts as "own". The running home reads the book every 5 s (the CLI writes it from another process), checks each way from itself every 5 min by the same challenge, and calls a way up whenever a device is connected through it now (a machine often can't open its own ts.net name). The list goes to every client and worker after each welcome and whenever it changes (`{t:"ways"}`); `lan` is reserved for step 4 and nothing adds it. **(5) Devices pick their way.** The rules are one module (`packages/protocol/src/reach.ts`, mirrored in Go, Swift and Kotlin): nearest first (same network, tailnet, domain, tunnel; then the primary), each tried 250 ms after the one before, the first that proves it is the home wins unless a better one still pending answers within 300 ms; while connected, a look every 30 s at the way in use and every better one: leave a way only after two misses in a row (for the best one that answered), move up only after a better one answered twice in a row. Workers do it on every redial and every 30 s, keeping their sessions through the switch (the grace); the CLI picks once per command for a home in `home.json`; the Mac app races at launch and runs the keeper every 30 s, retargeting its socket; the iPhone and Android apps race on coming to the front and when the page can't reach its home, and every 30 s only leave a way that stopped answering (a move reloads the page, so moving up waits for the front). The iPhone and Android apps keep the device record (token in the Keychain, or the app's own storage on Android; device id and name) so a page opened at another origin asks the app for it (`{t:"device"}`) and is the same device. Android verifies Ed25519 from Android 13; before it the app stays on its one address. The web page stays on its own origin (storage, push and the service worker are bound to it) and lists the other addresses. Switching ways never needs pairing again. **(6) Devices says how.** A connected worker's and a client's card: the header **怎么连着 / How it's connected**, one row: **经由你的 Tailscale 网络 / Through your tailnet** · **经由你的域名 / Through your domain** · **经由你的 Cloudflare 通道 / Through your Cloudflare tunnel** · **同一个网络 / Same network** · **就在这台电脑上 / On this same computer**, its muted line **全程加密，中间谁也看不到 / Encrypted all the way; nobody in between can read it**, through Cloudflare (a tunnel, or a domain behind Cloudflare's proxy) **加密到 Cloudflare 为止，Cloudflare 能看到内容 / Encrypted as far as Cloudflare, which can read it**, plain http on a network **没有加密，同一个网络里的人能看到 / Not encrypted; others on the network can read it**, on the home's own computer **不经过网络 / Never leaves this computer**. The home reads it off the request that opened the socket (its Host against the book; Tailscale serve's and Cloudflare's own headers), so it needs nothing from the device and works with every client version. The home's card: **能连到 {home} 的地址 / Addresses that reach {home}**, a row per way: the kind (**Tailscale 网络 / Tailscale network** · **你的域名 / Your domain** · **Cloudflare 通道 / Cloudflare tunnel** · **同一个网络 / Same network**) over its address, and at the right **连得上 / Reachable** · **连不上 / Can't reach** · **还没查过 / Not checked yet** · **在用 / In use** (the way this window uses); under it, with a tunnel, **经过 Cloudflare 通道的内容，Cloudflare 能看到。其他地址全程加密。/ Cloudflare can read what goes through its tunnel. The other addresses are encrypted all the way.**, and on the web **这个页面一直用打开它的地址……/ This page stays on the address it was opened at…**. Each fact is its own element (D291), the D273 row anatomy, Mac and web. **(7) `ducter reach`** (a machine command, like `ducter domain`): `list` (default; each checked from here, the fingerprint said), `add <address> [--kind]`, `remove <address>`, `primary <address>`; `--json`. Extending `ducter domain`/`ducter tailscale` alone wouldn't cover an address set up by hand (a reverse proxy of your own, ZeroTier), which used to mean writing `public-url`. *Compatibility:* a 0.0.60 client with a D293 home: the link's code still parses, `public-url` still leads, the unknown frames are ignored (the Mac app logs and skips them), its sockets are pinged at the protocol level, which every WebSocket answers. A D293 client with a 0.0.60 home: no `ping` in the welcome (no deadline), no `fp` (no switching; one address as before), a worker's `held` is ignored (sessions end as before); a worker's pings were already answered. *Rejected:* a fixed 30 s ping (the D293 15/45 s gives three chances, as the systems in research/97 §4 do); letting the web page move origins (it would lose its storage and push); a probe that trusts an address without the key (a LAN address or a lapsed domain could be anyone's); moving up mid-use in the phone apps (a reload under the person's thumb). | U (the author asked for research/97's first three steps, 2026-11-16), A | `packages/protocol/src/{reach,reach-verify,index,internal,transcript}.ts`, `packages/core/src/{home-key,reach-book,workers,ws,core,devices,auth,anywhere}.ts`, `packages/runner/src/{remote,runner,worker-host}.ts`, `packages/cli/src/{uplink,worker,reach-cmd,tailscale,domain,remote,home,main,args,i18n}.ts`, `apps/web/src/{conn,app,main,native,devcard,transcript,i18n}.ts(x)`, `apps/web/static/app.css`, `apps/desktop/{main.go,internal/{client,remote,protocol,local,views,i18n}}`, `apps/ios/Ducter/{Store,WebShell,DucterApp}.swift`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/co/nowledge/ducter/android/{Reach,Store,Core,MainActivity}.kt`, tests, `design/{system,product-model,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/{phone,install,devices}.md` |

| D299 | **Built 2026-11-17 (core, runner, protocol, the web wide and phone, the Mac app), checked with synthetic sessions in the installed agents' own record shapes and fake runtimes; not yet against a real model or a real person's sessions.** *Who:* the heavy developer whose last month of Claude Code and Codex sessions (and pi's) sits in `~/.claude`, `~/.codex` and `~/.pi`, outside Ducter, and who wants to find "the Raft snapshot one" and carry on in Ducter, not start over; the consumer who used Claude Code by hand once and finds that afternoon in the same place; the fresh user who has no such sessions and never sees the section. *Feel:* before, moving to Ducter meant leaving every earlier conversation behind (D45 said start fresh); after, the first open of Past tasks already holds their own work, under **也在这台电脑上 / Also on this computer**, and one tap carries the very conversation on, with its earlier turns above. *First time:* nothing to turn on; the section is there in Past tasks when such sessions exist, with one quiet line saying what it is. **(1) Shown by default, read lazily and locally.** Read only when Past tasks asks, on the home, only each file's head and tail (sessions reach a GB, research/103 §4), kept until the file changes; never sent anywhere but the person's own clients; never read by a model to list. Ducter's own sessions are never listed (their ids are in the Log; its data folder, the Ducter folder and temporary folders are left out); a session carried on already is listed as its task. The ⋯ menu's **不再显示 {agent} 的 / Don't show {agent} here** hides one agent for good (`outside.json` on the home, every window told); the section's last line **不显示的：{agents} / Not shown: {agents}** with **再显示 / Show again** brings it back. Chosen over opt-in (a setting the heavy developer would turn on in the first minute anyway, and the consumer never finds) and over an import step (copies the person would then have two of). **(2) Found by D285's search.** The same field, time words and agent and project chips find a session by its name (the person's `/rename`, Claude Code's own title, pi's `--name`), the person's first and last words, its folder and project (a worktree another agent workbench made counts as its repo), its branch and its agent; every word must match; starred and tags narrow to Ducter's tasks only. **(3) The card** is D285's: the picture guessed from its words by the same rule as a task's, its name, the person's first words (or where the words matched), and one small line of project, agent, branch and day, each its own word (no " · " joins, D291); a folder no longer there says **文件夹不在了 / Folder gone** and can't be carried on. **(4) 接着做 / Continue** makes it a Ducter task working in the session's own folder directly (no copy: the person worked there by hand and their own git is the undo), whose transcript opens with **在 {agent} 里开始的，{day} / Began in {agent} on {day}**, the last 60 turns of the conversation (the person's words and the agent's; tool calls stay in the session, which the agent reads itself), then the hairline **{time} 在 Ducter 里接着做 / Picked up in Ducter at {time}**. The same agent resumes that very session by its id (Claude Code `--resume`, Codex `thread/resume`, pi by id in its folder, through OAR), told where it came from; it appends to its own file as it does by hand, and Ducter never writes that file. **换一个 agent 接着做 / Continue with another agent** starts the other agent in the same folder from what the session said (D282's condensed start: the person's last words to it and its last words); a resume the agent refuses falls back to the same. Again on the same session opens its task. The partner hears a quiet note; its Past card says **从 {agent} 接过来的 / Carried on from {agent}**. **(5) One reader for two features:** `packages/core/src/local-agents/` lists projects and sessions and summarizes one, for this and D298's first greeting. *Not taken:* forking the session (`--fork-session`) so the original file stays byte-for-byte (two copies of one conversation, and by hand the person would no longer find Ducter's turns); importing every session into the Log (gigabytes of tool output, privacy for nothing). *Open (todo):* a worker's sessions (an op over the worker link), Codex's own thread names from its database, New task from this for an outside session, a real-model run of a resume. Partly supersedes D45 and the roadmap's "Not planned: taking over sessions you started outside" | U (the author: research/100's first-hour gaps, item 4; the brief of 2026-11-17), L, research/103 | `research/103-agent-sessions.md`, `packages/core/src/local-agents/{index,agents,read}.ts`, `packages/core/src/outside.ts`, `packages/core/src/{past,ws,core,registry}.ts`, `packages/runner/src/{runner,brief}.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/{past,index,internal,transcript}.ts`, `packages/core/test/{local-agents,outside}.test.ts`, `packages/core/test/fixtures-agents.ts`, `packages/runner/test/adopt.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/{past.tsx,transcript.tsx,app.ts,i18n-past.ts,i18n-transcript.ts}`, `apps/web/static/app.css`, `apps/web/demo-outside.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/{pastoutside,past,transcript,taskturns,tasksteps,taskpage,app}.go`, `apps/desktop/internal/{protocol/past.go,store/past.go,i18n/{past,turns,loop}.go}`, `design/{past,product-model,onboarding,roadmap,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/past-tasks.md` |
