## 2026-11-17: a usage limit is a wait, not a failure (research/100 item 3, research/101; scenario A4; principle 13)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D297 | **Built 2026-11-17 (runner, protocol, core, partner context, web, Mac) and checked by tests with each agent's limit shape from source (research/101), fake clocks and fake runtimes, a home restart and the hand-off; not yet against a real limit hit on any account, on a worker, or by a person.** *Who:* the heavy developer whose overnight tasks stopped when Claude Code's 5-hour window ran out (before: a failed turn, a task that read 在做 until morning, nothing done); the consumer, who never hears the word limit unless it matters; the fresh user, who sees a ring and one sentence. *Feel:* before, a limit was a failure from nowhere; after, 放心: it says when it carries on and does, by itself, in the same session. *First time:* the first limit any task meets; nothing to set up. **(1) Detection, in the runner** (`limit-hit.ts`): a failed turn OAR classes `quota` (or `rate_limited`, a throttle that outlived the agent's own retries) is a limit, never an error line; its reset, best first: OAR's `resetsAt` (Claude Code's `rate_limit_event`), the used-up window the session said just before (Claude Code's event as read by D288, Codex's `account/rateLimits/updated`), the agent's own words (Codex "try again at 3:12 PM" / "Nov 18th, 2026 3:12 PM", Claude Code "resets 3am (Asia/Shanghai)" and "usage limit reached\|<unix s>"), else unknown. The runner logs one line (`raw.limit`), no nudge; the failed turn says nothing of its own. **(2) The default: wait and carry on** (`core/limits.ts`): the task rests on a wait of its own (D267's `wakes: "task"` timer with `limit`), at the reset plus a minute's grace, and then gets **{agent} 的额度恢复了，接着做刚才没做完的。** in the same native session (resumed by id, D282), a home restart included (the wait is in the Log; overdue, it carries on at once). No reset known: it tries again (10 minutes after a throttle, else hourly, at most a day, then the person's turn). **(3) One account, one reset:** a task whose agent named no time takes the reset another task on that account was given, and a newly named reset moves the rest; On hand draws two or more under one line, **Claude Code 的额度 3:12 恢复 / Claude Code's limit resets 3:12** with **这 3 件到时一起接着做 / These 3 carry on together then**, each task still its own card. **(4) The card** (D279's look: the clay ring filling toward the reset, the time left inside): **Claude Code 的额度用完了 / Claude Code's limit is used up**, **额度 3:12 恢复，到时接着做 / The limit resets at 3:12, and it carries on then** (unknown: **额度恢复后接着做，4:10 先去试一次 / It carries on once the limit is back, and tries again at 4:10**), then **现在换 Codex 接着做 / Hand it to Codex now** (only when another signed-in agent on the same computer can take it: not limited itself, not paid per use, D89) through D282's in-task switch, carrying the task's progress, and **先停下 / Stop here** (the wait ends, the task is the person's turn; 不等了 and Stop waiting not taken: D279's raters read "stop waiting" as deleted, and the result is that it stops). The state word everywhere is **额度 3:12 恢复 / Limit resets 3:12**, the row's line **等 Claude Code 的额度恢复 / Waiting until Claude Code's limit resets** (in the viewer's language, from the agent, not the logged reason), the transcript's hairlines **Claude Code 的额度用完了 / Claude Code's limit ran out** with **额度 3:12 恢复** apart, and **Claude Code 的额度恢复了，接着做 / Claude Code's limit came back, carrying on** with its time apart (D291); the end line **等 Claude Code 的额度恢复** with **额度 3:12 恢复** apart. **(5) Hand off automatically** is the person's choice, made where it matters: a quiet switch under the card's buttons, **以后额度用完，直接换别的 AI agent 接着做 / Next time a limit runs out, hand it to another AI agent right away** (`Settings.limitHandoff`, off by default; not a Settings pane, D296's panes are another change). On, a limit with someone to take it is handed over at once (no wait; the transcript says the limit ran out, then D282's **换成 Codex 接着做**). **(6) The partner only when it matters:** a limit wait never wakes it, except once when no reset is known and nobody else can take the task (`limit.tell`); it reads the waits and their end in its context, and is told to mention one that happened while the person was away with the task's result ("昨晚 Claude Code 额度用完，3:12 恢复后接着做完了"). *Defaults the author may revisit:* hand-off off by default (an automatic move to another agent changes who works on the person's code); a minute's grace after a reset; unknown resets tried hourly for a day; pay-per-use agents never offered (they cost money; D89 says so before anything costs). *Alternative not taken:* hand off by default (faster, but a silent change of agent at 3 am on someone's repo is the kind of surprise principle 14 forbids). *Not built (todo):* the partner's own limit (its harness hitting one); a worker's limit read from its own account; an eval scenario for the morning line; OAR upstream carrying Codex's reset. | research/100, research/101, A | `packages/runner/src/{limit-hit,normalize,runner}.ts`, `packages/runner/test/limits.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/{limits,waiters,work,core,ws,settings}.ts`, `packages/core/test/limits.test.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/{index,transcript}.ts`, `packages/protocol/fixtures/{transcript-cases.ts,transcript.json}`, `packages/partner/src/{render,partner}.ts`, `apps/web/src/{i18n-limits,i18n,work,onhand,transcript,app}.ts(x)`, `apps/web/static/app.css`, `apps/web/{demo,demo-limits}.ts`, `apps/web/test/limits.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/{i18n/limits.go,i18n/limits_test.go,protocol/protocol.go,views/{limits,limitcard_test,work,onhandlist,onhandboard,taskpage,taskturns,transcript}.go}`, `design/{product-model,focus-window,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/waiting-and-routines.md`, `research/101-limits.md` |

## 2026-11-17: the partner's real first words, and a pasted key instead of a subscription (research/100 items 1 and 2: "the partner's first words are an empty state"; "no way in without a Claude or ChatGPT plan, short of a terminal"; research/102)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D298 | **Built 2026-11-17 on the home, the CLI, the Mac and the web, checked with fakes (a scratch home holding fake Claude Code and Codex records, a fake network for every key check) and in shots (`.shots/d298/mac`, `.shots/d298/web`, zh and en, wide and phone); not yet run with a real key or on a real first install; for the author's review.** *Who:* all three. The heavy developer opens Ducter for the first time and finds a partner that already knows what they were doing yesterday in their own agents; the consumer with no Claude or ChatGPT plan, often in China with a DeepSeek or Kimi key, gets in without a terminal; the fresh user gets a warm hello and everyday things to say, and, when nothing can think yet, one field. *Feel:* before, a greeting drawn by the app that the partner never said and knew nothing about, and for a key holder a dead end ("coming soon; put it in the key file"); after, the partner's own first message, specific within a second, and "paste a key" with an answer in its voice (wrong key, no balance, needs a proxy from here) in two or three seconds. *First time:* there is nothing to learn: the first words arrive by themselves, a tap fills the composer, and the key field says which keys work and that the key stays on this computer. (1) **The first words are a message, said by the home.** When an app (the Mac, the web, a phone) first says hello to a conversation that has never had a word in it, the home appends one `ai_msg` from the partner (`packages/core/src/first-words.ts`) before the hello's events go out, in the hello's language, with `first: {starts, looked?}`. No model runs (nothing may be signed in yet, and the first second costs nothing). The words are per-language tables picked by the hello's language (D292; a language without a table gets English). The text: a greeting by the person's hour in the partner's name, then, when the person's own agents have recent records, **我看了看这台电脑上你的 Claude Code 和 Codex 最近在做的事，这几件要不要接着来？ / I had a look at what your Claude Code and Codex worked on lately on this computer. Want to pick one of these up?**, else the everyday line; when nothing can think yet, one more sentence saying so and how (sign in, or paste a key below). The starts: up to three from the records, one per folder, newest first, each **{今天/昨天/n 天前/上周}你在 {folder} 里做「{title}」，要我接着看看吗？ / {When} you were on “{title}” in {folder}. Want me to pick it up?** (the title is Claude Code's summary or the name the person gave it, Codex's thread name, else the person's first words there, cut at a word), whose tap fills the composer with **接着 {folder} 里「{title}」这件事：先看看它停在哪儿，再跟我说下一步。（文件夹：{~/path}）/ Pick up “{title}” in {folder}: see where it stopped, then tell me the next step. (Folder: {~/path})** and never sends; then one everyday example (three when there are no records). It is in the Log, so the partner knows it said it (its context shows what was offered); said once (a second app sees the same message). Mem's line about the person is a hook (`FirstWordsInput.memLine`), left for D295. (2) **D204's "no scan" holds; reading the agents' own records is not a scan** (amends D204 (2)'s "No scanning anywhere" only for these records). D204 rejected guessing where code lives (a list of folders under `~/dev`, `~/code` … that the person must correct). The records Claude Code and Codex keep are not a guess: they are the exact folders the person chose to work in, written by tools the person runs, about work the person did; Ducter exists to carry that work on. Read only, through D299's reader of those records (`packages/core/src/local-agents/`, shared with Past tasks; `recentFolders` in `first-words.ts` picks from it): file names and times, and from each of the newest 40 files of the last 14 days per agent its folder, title and first words (head and tail, bounded); never inside the folders themselves; Ducter's own sessions (its data folder, its Ducter folder) and temporary folders left out; never sent anywhere except as the first words, which go where the person's own words go, to the model they chose. **On by default, with a one-tap no in place**: under the starts, **从这台电脑上你的 {agents} 留下的记录里看到的：只在这里读，只给你看。/ Found in what your {agents} keep on this computer: read here, shown only to you.** and **别再看了 / Stop looking** (`local_agents` frame, `settings.json` `localAgents: false`): the starts from the records go at once, the line becomes **好，以后不再看这些记录。/ Fine, I won't look at those records again.** with **还是看吧 / Look again**; with it off the first words never read them. Alternatives: ask before looking (a question before the first hello is a form, and for most people the answer is yes; the visible no right under what was read keeps the person in control); never look (the partner's first words stay generic, research/100 item 1). (3) **The clay partner over its first words**, while nothing else was said: the empty screen's character, waving once (still under reduced motion), then the bubble, then the starts two to a row (one on a phone). No "new" line over it. (4) **Paste a key, no subscription needed.** Recognised by shape (`packages/protocol/src/api-keys.ts`, research/102 §1): Anthropic, a Claude Code sign-in token, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi (China and international), Alibaba Model Studio, Zhipu GLM and Z.ai, Google Gemini, xAI, Groq; a plain `sk-` key is a list of candidates, settled by the check. **Checked with one call that spends nothing** (`packages/core/src/api-key.ts`, research/102 §2): the account's balance (DeepSeek, Kimi, OpenRouter), the key's own record or the model list, at the address the agent will use; the first candidate that knows the key wins. This replaces "one cheap call through pi": a model call spends tokens and seconds, needs pi to run already, and doesn't separate a wrong key from an empty account. **Kept** in `keys.env` (0600) under the variable its agent reads (`writeKey`), never in the Log, never printed, never sent back; **thought with**: DeepSeek Harness for a DeepSeek key when it is installed, else pi (Claude Code for an Anthropic key or token when it is installed), and, when nothing on that computer could think before, the partner's brain becomes that agent and the provider's model (`brainFromKey`; a choice the person made stays). A Model Studio key is said to be right but not usable yet (pi has no plain Model Studio provider; not kept). **The partner's words for every result** (`keyWords`, both languages, sent with the result): works; works but this computer needs pi (pi's own installer, opened in Terminal, since it asks before installing Node); not a key; wrong key; no balance; too many requests; can't reach a provider abroad from here (with a proxy suggested and DeepSeek, Kimi or Zhipu named); no network; not usable yet. (5) **Where the key goes in:** the Mac's first run, under the agents to install and sign in (**或者，贴一个 API 密钥 / Or paste an API key**, **不用订阅：按用量付费的密钥也行。/ No subscription needed: a key you pay for by use works too.**, then the card), through `ducter key add --json` with the key on stdin; a good key makes the check run again and the first run goes on by itself. In the conversation (Mac and web) whenever nothing on the home can think (`first_screen.noBrain`): under the first words, else above the composer; the `key_add` frame. Settings and Devices are D296's (a todo). (6) **D102 amended: pi gets the DeepSeek key too** (it signs in with it, as DeepSeek Harness does), and the Kimi and GLM variables pi reads; still never Claude Code or Codex. `ducter doctor` no longer counts a key for pi as a way in unless pi can run here (node or pi), and then says **密钥已经收好了，装上 pi 就能用 / your key is kept; install pi to use it** with pi's installer. Persona and partner tools unchanged (no D175 eval); the partner's projection shows what the first words offered. | U (the request, research/100), L (research/102) | `packages/protocol/src/{api-keys,keys,harnesses,index}.ts`, `packages/core/src/{first-words,api-key,ws,core,main,settings}.ts`, `packages/partner/src/render.ts`, `packages/cli/src/{key-cmd,args,home,main,doctor,i18n}.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/{protocol/firstwords.go,protocol/protocol.go,store/store.go,i18n/firstwords.go,local/addkey.go}`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/{firstwords,conversation,onboard,setup,app}.go`, `apps/web/src/{first-words.tsx,i18n-first.ts,i18n.ts,store.ts,views.tsx}`, `apps/web/static/app.css`, `apps/web/demo-first.ts`, tests `packages/protocol/test/api-keys.test.ts`, `packages/core/test/{api-key,first-words,key-add,fake-agents}.ts`, `packages/cli/test/key-cmd.test.ts`, `packages/runner/test/child-env.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/firstwords_test.go`, `design/{onboarding,product-model,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/{faq,getting-started,install}.md`, research/102 |

## 2026-11-17: 替你做过的 / Done for you, the record of what Ducter did on the person's behalf (research/100 item 8; scenario G5; principle 18; research/104)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D300 | **Built 2026-11-17 (protocol, core, the partner's tool, the web wide and phone, the Mac app), checked with a seeded day and fakes, and the partner eval's two new scenarios on haiku; not yet against real accounts.** *Who:* the developer at the end of a day of eight tasks ("did anything merge, touch an account?"), the consumer who gave it mail, a card and a phone ("what did it send in my name, what did it pay?"), the fresh user who meets it as a quiet line and usually sees the empty day first. *Felt:* 放心 above all: everything it did in their name in one short list, each with the Go they gave. (1) **The place: 替你做过的 / Done for you** (zh title, link and the Mac menu 替你做过的… / Done for You…, ⌘⇧Y), a whole-window place on the Mac and a sheet on the web like Past tasks; not a Settings pane. Reached from On hand's end (beside 做过的事 ›), one quiet line under the morning note, the Mac's menu, and the partner. Rejected names: 它替你做过的 (the partner has its own name; "it" adds nothing), 对外记录 / Outside record (a system word), 账本 / Ledger (money only). (2) **What counts:** only what left the task's own place or used something of the person's: sent (mail and messages through an account, a send or post tapped in an app after its Go, a message to another agent over Bridge), paid (a saved card after Pay, a pay or buy tap), called (every call placed, with how it ended), sign-ins and fills (saved sign-ins and details, keys given), changed (calendar, merge, draft PR, a folder task's files, a setting or install in an app, any other account write), deleted, and looked at (each account per day and task, **counts only, never content**). Not in it: the partner's own replies, work inside a task's own place, anything held or failed before it went out. A send never confirmed says 没确认送到 / Not confirmed; a call no one answered 没人接 / No answer. (3) **One card per action:** a drawn glyph per kind on a clay pebble, the line from a table by kind (发邮件给 {to} / Mailed {to} …), the thing's own words under it (≤ 140 chars), then each fact its own element (D291): who asked (你让它做的 / You asked · 任务「…」 · 例行「…」), the Go (你点了好 {time} / You said Go at {time} · 没人回，按默认做了 · 之前允许过), where (在 {device} 上 · Ducter 的手机 · 用 {line} 的号码 · 用你自己的号码 · 通过 {account}); 打开任务 / Open the task, 看结果 / See it, and **改回去 / Undo only where one truly exists** (a folder task's copy, D142). (4) **Days like a diary**, newest first, each with its counts as separate facts; a field that searches as you type; filters by kind with counts; 更早的 / Earlier adds a week; the honest coverage line at the end (commands a task ran directly on its computer aren't here). **The empty day:** the clay character with its notebook, 今天没有替你发出、付过或打过什么。/ Nothing sent, paid or called for you today., and what did happen as facts. (5) **Nothing new is stored:** the record is derived at read time from the Log and Autofill's uses (`core/src/did.ts`); protocol `did` → `did_result` (`protocol/src/did.ts`). (6) **The partner answers from the same list:** a read-only tool `did_list` (when: today / yesterday / week; kind), actions kept apart from the counts of looks; one persona line ("asked what you did for them: did_list first, with the kind"). | # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |

Warm dark paper (`#17120E`, surfaces `#231C16`/`#2A221B`, brown-black, never grey); every card and button keeps its ledge (a near-black base, `#0D0A07`); the ink button turns cream with dark words on a taupe ledge; the quiet button keeps the paper with a faint light rim; each state's surface goes deep and its ink light, its dot keeping its hue; the tints are `MidnightTints`; the Devices sea goes to dusk (same scene, the light low and warm); the picture viewer and the title moment were already dark. Clay art is cut out and reads as it is; the Codex coin, whose charcoal knot would vanish, takes its D213 dark cast (`coin_codex_dark`, the web's, 128 px: the coins draw at 64 pt or less) through `theme.Clay`, which gives an asset's `_dark` cast while the window is dark. No view hard-codes a colour (a grep found only brand marks on app tiles, the sea's alpha shadows and the title's black, all theme-independent by design). **(2) The setting.** Settings › 外观和声音 / Look and sound › 外观 / Look gains **浅色和深色 / Light and dark**: **跟随系统 / Follow the system** (the default; the glossary's word, the same as the Language row under it, not a new "跟着系统 / Match the system"), **浅色 / Light**, **深色 / Dark**, under the Pebble row; D296's layout kept. Kept in the Mac's own `desktop.json` (this Mac only, like Language); it also sets MyGo's `Theme.SetSource`, so the menus, the title bar and the window's first paint (`light-dark(#FFF6EA, #17120E)`) agree. **(3) The change.** Live: MyGo re-renders on macOS's appearance change and the window reads it each frame. Every colour moves from one paper to the other at once over 360 ms on an ease in and out (`theme.Blend`, `AppearDur`), the way a room's light changes: no second copy of the page drawn over it; at once under Reduce Motion. **(4) Contrast (WCAG 2.x, `theme/contrast_test.go` fails below AA in dark; light / dark):** Ink on Bg 14.7 / 15.8, on Surface 15.7 / 14.3; InkSoft on Bg 9.8 / 11.7, on Surface 10.5 / 10.6; InkMuted on Bg 5.3 / 6.4, on Surface 5.6 / 5.8, on SurfaceSunken 4.6 / 6.1; Ink on Chrome 15.2 / 15.4; the user's bubble 6.7 / 6.7; the partner's bubble 15.7 / 13.3; on the accent 6.7 / 6.7; the ink button's words 14.7 / 15.8; highlight 6.3 / 7.6; added 7.5 / 9.1; deleted 8.5 / 9.1; a reply's quote on the partner 4.4 / 5.9, on the user's orange 3.5 / 5.4; the viewer's bar 17.2 / 18.7; state inks on their surfaces: needs you 6.4 / 9.3, working 7.8 / 9.8, waiting 6.7 / 10.8, done 6.6 / 10.1, failed 7.1 / 8.7, awake 6.6 / 10.1, asleep 7.8 / 9.2, away 6.2 / 8.8 (each on the paper 6.9–14.4); tint inks on their grounds 5.2–6.9 / 6.5–7.2; big numbers in Strong (3:1) 3.1–4.8 / 6.7–9.2. ## 2026-11-17: WeChat as a window on the one conversation, through WeChat's own ClawBot (research/100 item 7: "no chat window for Chinese users"; research/105; research/79 §2)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D301 | **Built 2026-11-17 (protocol, core, the web wide and phone, the Mac app), checked against a fake iLink and a fake CDN only; never on a real WeChat account.** *Who:* the consumer in mainland China whose life is in WeChat and who can't reach Telegram; the heavy developer in China whose phone is WeChat; the fresh user, who knows "扫一扫" and nothing else. *Felt before:* the partner lives only in the Ducter app. *After:* 放心 first: nobody signs in as them and their WeChat account risks nothing; 好用: one scan, nothing to paste; 顺滑: the same conversation in the app they already open; honest about what WeChat allows. (1) **The route is WeChat's own ClawBot over iLink**, the one official way for a person's own agent to talk with them in WeChat: a QR scan binds a one-to-one ClawBot contact to the scanner, the home long-polls (no public address), no real-name step for one's own binding. Never unofficial protocols or hooks that log in as the person (their whole social life and WeChat Pay at stake); WeCom's long-connection bot, Official Accounts and self-built WeCom apps are not this (in WeCom, or a business and a public domain). (2) **Ducter's own client of the documented protocol** (`channels/wechat.ts`); Tencent's MIT package was read for the protocol, nothing of it is used or run. It says who it is: `bot_agent: Ducter/<version>`, `channel_version: 2.4.10-ducter` (the protocol's version first, as its document asks of other hosts). (3) **The scan is the pairing:** `confirmed` names the scanner (`ilink_user_id`), who becomes the one linked account; nobody else can add the ClawBot, and anyone else's words are still ignored (D276 (5)). No code to type; WeChat's own number is passed on when it asks; a QR that runs out is replaced three times, then Settings says the QR ran out and that their WeChat may not have ClawBot yet. Unlink is Disconnect. (4) **It answers, it doesn't push:** caps `replyWindowMs` (23 h) and `windowSends` (9), both a little under what is reported (about 24 h, about 10, secondhand). Anything, a turn's answer or what Ducter starts itself, goes to WeChat only inside that window; outside it the place falls back to the app and push carries it. WeChat refusing a send closes the window until the person writes. (5) **No buttons, no edits:** a reversible card ends with 回「好」就{go}，回「先等等」就先放着。/ Reply "ok" to {go}, or "wait" to hold it. (the hub's typed words); Open in Ducter carries the home's address written out when it has one; no Still on it line. (6) Pictures, files and video both ways through WeChat's AES-128-ECB CDN; voice comes in as WeChat's transcript. Replies carry the newest `context_token`; typing through `getconfig`/`sendtyping`. A stale token (-14) is Can't connect: 微信要你重新扫一次码。, never a retry loop. (7) **Settings › 聊天软件 gets a WeChat group** (between Slack and iMessage, the sage tint, 微 / W): off says 用微信自己的 ClawBot 连 with two steps; scan shows the QR (on a phone too, with the screenshot hint) and 不连了 / Cancel; linked says 和你的微信连着, whether it can reach them now, and the rule in one paragraph; its privacy line says it is WeChat's ClawBot and that Ducter never signs in to their WeChat. | research/105, research/79 §2, research/100 item 7, D276, D283 | `channels.md` §9, product-model glossary, scenarios H7, `docs/chat-apps.md`, todo |

## 2026-11-17: rich answers, a table, a chart, a list to tick or answers to tap in a reply (research/100 item 5: "answers are text only"; motivation.md "world-class generative UI")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D303 | **Built 2026-11-17 (protocol, the partner, the web wide and phone, the Mac app), checked with unit and fixture tests on both clients, the Mac test renderer, headless Chrome against a demo core, and the partner eval's five new `rich-*` scenarios on haiku with `--only` (the last two runs 5/5 and 4/5); the full eval is rerun at the merge (D175).** *Who:* the consumer who asks "compare these two" or "how did last week go" and got a paragraph of numbers; the developer asked "which repo?" who types its name; the fresh user, who must never meet markup. *Felt:* 好用 and 赏心悦目: a comparison or a week reads at a glance, a choice is one tap; 放心: the numbers are the real ones; nothing extra when a sentence will do. (1) **Four kinds, only when asked for:** a table (a comparison), a chart (bar or line, one series, numbers from a tool, a report or the person, never remembered or guessed), a checklist (a list to tick), choices (a question with 2–5 short answers; a tap sends that answer). Never for one fact, a yes/no, a greeting, a task's result, or anything needing Go: that stays a decision card (rule 7 now says "choices about the work"). Persona section "Rich answers" (about 1.5K characters; the budget ceiling raised to 24.2K). (2) **The format:** a fenced ```` ```ducter-ui ```` block of one JSON object (`type` table / chart / checklist / choices; the limits: 2–6 columns and 1–12 rows of cells up to 80 characters; 2–14 points with a required one-sentence `summary`; 1–12 items, `tell` to hear back; 2–5 distinct options up to 40 characters; 4000 characters a block, three a message, one choices). Rejected: tool calls (a block belongs in the words, where it stands; a tool adds a turn and a schema to every request), Markdown tables (no chart, no choice, unreadable in chat apps), HTML or a free component tree (a page, not a reply; unsafe; can't degrade). (3) **The home validates and degrades it** (`protocol/src/rich.ts` `parseRich`, in the partner's message path): a valid block is stored on the message (`ai_msg.ui`, with its `plain` text) and replaced in `text` by that plain text; a bad one is left out and counted (`uiDropped`), which the partner reads in its history; a message that would be empty keeps its JSON as code. So chat apps, pushes, Copy, memory and older clients all get one text that reads: a table one line per row, a chart its sentence and its points, a list or choices `- ` lines, with the reply language's punctuation (a `words()` table, D292). (4) **One drawing model on both clients:** a client splits the text at each block's plain text (`splitRich`; a block it can't find goes last, a kind it doesn't know stays as text) and draws from `richModel` / Go `ModelOf` (numeric columns; the chart's scale from zero to a round top in at most five steps of 1, 2 or 5; numbers with at most two decimals, grouped thousands; "%" and "°" hug, any other unit a space); `fixtures/rich.json` is passed by the web's model and the Go port. (5) **The look (Pebble, tokens only, light and dark):** the day card's white on its clay base; a table's head small and muted, row labels bold, numbers right-aligned in even figures, a wide one scrolling sideways in its card on a phone; bars in the accent clay with a lighter top and a ledge, a line in the accent with hollow points, a dashed line per step and the zero line solid, values over bars and points when eight or fewer; checklist boxes on a ledge, a ticked one in the done tint with its item struck through; choices as clay pills under the question. (6) **Behaviour:** a choice's tap sends its words as the person's own message (no pictures, no reply-to); choices work until the person says anything after the message, then stay as a record, theirs in the accent, the rest faded. Ticks stay on the device (web `localStorage`, the Mac's `desktop.json`); only `tell: true` adds **报一下进度 / Send progress**, which sends **勾好了：{done}。还没：{left}。/ Done: {done}. Not yet: {left}.** (or all / none) at any time. (7) **Accessibility:** a real table (headers by column and row; Mac table, row, header and cell roles); a chart is an image whose words are its sentence then each value (the web adds a hidden table); checklist items are checkboxes; choices a labelled group. | research/100 item 5, motivation.md, principles 7 and 20, D129, D222, D236, D254, D291, D292, D302 | `conversation.md` "Rich answers", product-model glossary, scenarios H8, roadmap, `docs/tables-and-charts.md`, todo |
## 2026-11-17: Nowledge Mem in the conversation, said quietly (D295's plan (a), (b), (d); memory.md "Deep integration")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D304 | **Built 2026-11-17 (protocol, partner, core, runner, the web wide and phone, the Mac), checked with fakes (a fake Mem, a fake corrector and forgetter, the fake clock), the partner eval's three new scenarios on haiku with `--only`, and shots against the demo core (`DEMO_RECALL=1`, `.shots/d304/web`, `.shots/d304/mac`: light and dark, zh and en); never against a real Mem; not yet reviewed by the author; the full eval is to be rerun at merge.** *Who:* the developer whose Claude Code and Codex already write to the same Mem (before: Ducter's knowing felt like a guess; after: one line says whose words it leaned on), the consumer who told it a preference once (after: it is visibly theirs, and fixable), the fresh user (nothing new to learn: a line under a message, a tap, a plain card). *Feel:* 放心 most: what it remembered is never hidden when it changed an answer, never paraded when it didn't. **(1) The 想起了 / Remembered line.** Under a reply (an ai_msg or an ack) a recalled memory changed, one quiet line in the muted ink with the partner's notebook: **想起了你 {date} 说的** (the person's words to the partner, Mem source `ducter`) · **想起了 {date} {tool} 记下的** (another AI tool) · **想起了 {date} 你记下的** (the person's own note); the date before the tool so "日记" never forms. Only when the recall changed the answer, at most one per reply, never a list of what it read, never the memory's text. Supersedes D295 (a)'s "in the reply's Details": inside Details nobody would see it, and the point is trust at the moment of the answer. **(2) The mechanism: a mark the code checks.** memory_search gives each result a short ref (`m1`, never Mem's id) and who saved it; its result note says: only if one of them changed what you say, end that message with its ref, `[[m1]]`. Code takes every mark out of the words before they are logged (no client, chat app or the Log ever sees one), resolves the first against this turn's results only (an invented or stale ref makes no line), and logs one `memory_recalled` (memoryId, title, by, from, date, aboutSeq) right after the message; a mark said alone goes under the words before it. Chosen over a new tool (a call per answer, ≈0.4K in every session's prefix, latency) and over a reply tool the partner doesn't have; the tool list and the persona are unchanged. **(3) Tapped:** 它想起的这条 / What it remembered: the title, who it is from and the date as separate facts (D291), **这次的回答用到了它。**, **忘掉 / Forget** asking in place (another tool's: **…，{tool} 那边也一样。**: forgetting is Mem's and reaches every tool; D295's read-only for other tools' memories now holds for Settings only), and **在 Nowledge Mem 里打开 / Open in Nowledge Mem** (Mem's site; no documented link to one memory yet, todo). A forgotten line disappears on every client (`MemView.forgotten`). **(4) 这周记下的 / What it learned this week.** The week's first morning note (Monday's, or the first after a Monday it missed) carries one line, **这周记下了 {n} 件关于你的事，要看看对不对吗？** with **看看**, when it noted anything in the last 7 days and memory is on; never in the notification; a quiet Monday still shows it (without a push). No Sunday-evening note: the morning note is the one place it speaks unasked (D250). The sheet: each line **对** (kept as checked), **改** (the person's words; `nmem m update --title --content` through the partner's Mem client; **改好了，Nowledge Mem 里那条也改了。** or, without an id or when Mem refuses, **这里改好了；Nowledge Mem 里那条没改成。**), **忘掉** (asks). **(5) Other tools' memories in task briefs.** At a task's start the existing recall (title + brief, 4 hits) now also runs where the person's Mem plugin is there; then only other AI tools' memories are named, ≤ 3, by id, tool and title, in `<from_your_other_tools>`, for the agent to read through its own plugin (the person's own memories come from the plugin; contents never travel). Where Ducter's recall stands in, `<what_i_know>` lines say **saved by {tool}**. **(6) Measured** (haiku, `--only`): the three new scenarios pass (recall used → one line by "said"; another tool's → one line by "tool"; a general question → none), and `mem-recall-last-time-zh`'s ack got its line unasked; `mem-recall-person-en` (length) and `mem-down-zh` fail as they did before this change on haiku. | U (the D304 brief), D295, D250, D168 | `memory.md` "In the conversation (D304)", product-model glossary, scenarios J12, `docs/settings.md`, todo; `packages/partner/src/{partner,memory}.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/mem-source.ts`, `packages/core/src/{settings,ws}.ts`, `packages/core/src/proactive/engine.ts`, `packages/runner/src/{brief,runner}.ts`, `apps/web/src/recall.tsx`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/recall.go` |

## 2026-11-17: voice, first slice: hold to talk and read aloud with each device's own speech (research/100 item 6: "no voice"; scenario H2; research/106)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D305 | **Built 2026-11-17 (protocol helpers, the web wide and phone, the Mac app, the iPhone and Android shells' bridge), checked only with fakes: a fake recognizer and voice in unit tests on the web and the Mac, the shared helpers' fixture on both, Android's pure-logic tests, the iOS shell built for the simulator, shots of the web in headless Chrome against the demo core (`?voice-fake`) and of the Mac in its test renderer (`.shots/d305/`), zh and en, light and dark. Never with a real microphone, recognizer or voice on any platform; not yet reviewed by the author.** *Who:* the consumer used to holding a mic in a messaging app (before: a long thought typed with one thumb; after: said in ten seconds, read back before it goes); the heavy developer at the Mac (holds a key, talks a paragraph of context, edits, sends); the fresh user (a mic where every messaging app has one; one line on first use says why and where the sound goes). *Feel:* 好用 one gesture; 顺滑 words appear as heard; 赏心悦目 the clay partner leans in, a calm meter; 放心 listens only while held, says plainly where the sound goes, the home never receives audio; 惊喜 replies read back while talking by voice. **(1) Hold to talk** in the conversation's composer on every client (not a task's composer yet): a drawn microphone before Send; hold to listen; let go puts the words into the box after what is typed (`joinHeard`), not sent; slide up ≥ 56 pt sends at once; slide left ≥ 72 pt drops; sliding back disarms; a tap (< 250 ms) says **要按住说，松开就好。**; nothing heard says **没听清，再说一次？**; Esc drops. The Mac also holds a key while Ducter is in front (Settings › 外观和声音 › 语音 › 按住说话的键: Fn, 右边的 Option (the default: macOS uses it for nothing alone), 不用键), with a line for Fn when macOS's own dictation also takes it; no global key, no Input Monitoring. **(2) The engines are the platform's own** (research/106): the Speech framework and AVSpeechSynthesizer on the Mac (through purego) and the iPhone (the shell), SpeechRecognizer and TextToSpeech on Android (the shell), the Web Speech API in a browser. The device first: `requiresOnDeviceRecognition` where Apple supports the language, Android's on-device recognizer on API 31+, Chrome's `processLocally` when its pack is installed, `localService` voices first. Rejected: D218's realtime loop (a paid cloud model with the person's key; it stays for calls and a later full conversation) and Ducter's own model (a download and a GPU for what every device already has). **(3) Language:** the conversation's (D292 `convLang`), else the interface's, as a full locale (`speechLocale`: a preferred locale of the same language wins, else its usual region; Traditional Chinese never zh-CN). **(4) First use, permission, unavailable:** the first hold shows one card (**用说的，不用打字**, **只在你按住的时候听，松开就停。**, the privacy line, **用麦克风 / 先不用**), then the OS asks; denied says **Ducter 现在不能用麦克风。** (or 语音识别) with **去设置里打开** where an app can open the place (the iPhone's and Android's app settings, the Mac's Privacy & Security), and the site-settings sentence in a browser; unavailable says **这里还不能用语音** and the reason (a browser without it, a language it doesn't know by its autonym, no microphone, not https, unreachable, an app too old, the microphone busy, the Mac app not run as the installed app). **(5) The privacy line** comes from what the engine reports: on this device; Apple's; Google's; this browser's (Chrome's is Google's); this phone's service. Never "on device" when the engine can't promise it. **(6) Read aloud:** **朗读 / Read aloud** in a partner message's menu (and a second hover pebble on a wide screen), **停止朗读 / Stop reading** under it while it reads; `speakable(text)` (no marks, links by their words, code skipped; D303 blocks are already plain text) in the message's own language (`readLang`); typing stops it. **用语音说的时候，把回复念出来 / Read replies aloud when I talk by voice**, off by default, per device (the web: Settings › 这台手机; the Mac: Settings › 外观和声音 › 语音): the reply to a message sent by voice is read once. **(7) Motion:** a strip over the composer (the words typed stay): the partner's clay face at 44 pt tilted toward the mic and leaning in, breathing slightly with the level; five accent bars from the level (`meterBars`, `smoothLevel`: up fast, down slow); in 180 ms, out 140 ms. Reduce Motion: the pose holds still and the meter is one dot whose opacity follows the level. **(8) The app bridge** (`voice.md`): `voice.can`, `voice.start`, `voice.stop`, `voice.cancel`, `voice.settings`, `speak`, `speak.stop`, events through `window.ducterVoice`; `ducterNative.voice = 1`. **(9) What is not yet so:** the Mac's Fn watcher (an NSEvent local monitor for keyCode 63) is built but no real key press has reached it; the Mac's strip leaves at once (no 140 ms exit) and has no hover speaker (Read aloud is in its menu); a probe on the build Mac made real recognizers without listening: zh-CN and en-US on the device, ja-JP through Apple. | research/100 item 6, research/106, D218, D254, D291, D292, D302, D303 | `voice.md`, product-model glossary, scenarios H2, `conversation.md`, roadmap, `docs/voice.md`, todo; `packages/protocol/src/voice.ts`, `apps/web/src/voice*.ts*`, `apps/desktop/internal/voice`, `apps/ios/Ducter/Voice.swift`, `apps/android/.../Voice.kt` |

## 2026-11-17: at a glance without opening the app (research/100 item 9: "ambient presence ends at the menu bar"; research/107)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D306 | **Built 2026-11-17 (protocol, core, the relay, the web phone client, the Mac app, the iPhone app and a widget extension, the Android app), checked with fakes (a fake APNs transport and relay, the fake clock, a fake app bridge), the Mac test renderer (the mark and a mock of the menu, light and dark, zh and en), the iOS Simulator (the Lock Screen views in a specimen, the Dynamic Island from a locally started activity) and Android unit tests; the iPhone's push-to-update path is behind a flag (`DUCTER_LIVE_ACTIVITIES`, off) until a real iPhone checks it; Android has no push from the home, so its glance lives while the app does; not yet reviewed by the author.** *Who:* the developer with eight tasks running who wants to know, without switching windows, whether any of them needs them (before: open the window or wait for a notification; after: the mark in the bar has a clay dot, or it doesn't); the consumer who asked Ducter to call the dentist and is now on the bus (after: the call's phase on the Lock Screen, 通话中, then 打完了, and it goes by itself); the fresh user, who meets a small pebble in the menu bar that looks like the partner and never shows a number. *Felt:* 放心 above all (it is minding things; it says when it needs you), and 好用 (no window to open to know). **What earns a glance, and what never does (first principles, research/107 §4):** whether anything needs the person, the one state that may draw the eye; whether something is at work, as quiet as the bar; one thing the person chose to keep in sight; a live call in their name. Never a count that grows with work (no number in the bar; the Dock badge stays D71's), never every task, never a sound for a change of phase, never a task's words on a Lock Screen, never a phase it can't vouch for. **(1) The Mac's menu bar extra (D71's) carries the whole.** Three states, no number: **quiet** (the pebble with its eyes, nothing at work and nothing for you; resting waits and finished work are quiet), **at work** (the eyes look down at the work; still a template image, tinted with the bar), **needs you** (the pebble in the bar's own ink with a soft clay dot at its shoulder, Pebble's accent `#FF8A3D`, a clear gap around it; never red; drawn for a light or a dark bar, `Tray.Dark()`). The menu: On hand's one sentence first (D287, counts and times only; also the tooltip), what needs you (D71's Go, Hold and Reply…, and **打开任务 / Open the Task** where it has one; a key or a pay code still opens the window, D233), then **打开 Ducter / Open Ducter**, **设置… / Settings…**, **不在菜单栏显示 / Don't Show in the Menu Bar**, Quit. D71's **等你 · {n}** and **没有要你定的事** header lines are replaced by the sentence. It goes away when it's done.**; a call that goes live while the app is open shows by itself, once (removed, it isn't put back). ## 2026-11-17: a routine run closes at its turn's end (research/108 B3: "routine tokens counted as 0 on Claude Code")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D308 | **Built 2026-11-17, checked with the fake clock and tests in the real order (report, then usage); not yet run live.** A routine run's *result* is set by its report (done or failed, the first one), but the run *closes* at its turn's end: its tokens are the usage that turn reports, or, if the residency leaves `hot` (or a turn end comes) without a usage line, what was seen so far. A reported run waits at most 2 minutes (`CLOSE_WAIT_MS`) for that, then closes with what it has; the next firing closes it first; a restart closes it on the way back with the usage already in the task's stream. Why: on Claude Code `report_to_main` is a call inside the turn, so the turn's usage comes after it; closing on the report recorded `tokens: 0`, so D114's per-run budget (2x the first run) was never set and the month's count stayed 0. The other option, counting usage after a closed run toward its month, was not taken: it loses the per-run record the per-run budget is built from. A run stopped by its own budget, or a task the person dropped, still closes at once. Alongside (research/108 N1): a rich table's or chart's plain form never doubles a part's own end punctuation with the separator after it ("…your app. Concurrency…", "一个文件。并发…"), in every language's punctuation table | research/108 B3, N1; D114; D303 | `packages/core/src/routines.ts`, `packages/core/test/routine-runs.test.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/rich.ts`, `packages/protocol/fixtures/rich-cases.ts` |

It replaces every fallback that only stripped `.local` (the home's name in the core seven times, the browser and phone hosts, Devices, the CLI's pairing name and computer, `ducter worker`, `ducter task --repo` on a remote home, `ducter update`, the headless banner, the Mac's `remote.DeviceName`). A name the person gave (`device-name`, `--name`, a rename) is never rewritten. **Matching:** `sameComputer` folds case and every character that isn't a letter or digit, so a Computer Name and its host name agree ("Wey’s MacBook Pro" ≡ "Weys-MacBook-Pro.local"): a task placed by another of a worker's names finds it when exactly one live worker matches (after id, name and former names), the app and the command line fold into one computer's card, and a rename can't take any of the home's names (the core, the CLI, the Mac's "this Mac" check with `ThisHost`). **Migration:** once per `devices.db` (`user_version` 1) a device paired under its host name with a domain is renamed without it ("Mac.lan" → "Mac", "CLI on Mac.lan" → "CLI on Mac", numbered if taken), the old name kept as a former name (D84), and its computer loses the domain too; a computer from an older Ducter that pairs now is cleaned as it pairs; both clients show any such name without the domain (`shownDeviceName`, `store.ShownDeviceName`, the web's place name). *Tradeoff:* a person-chosen worker name that looks like a host ("build.box" at pairing) loses its dot; a rename afterwards keeps it. *Alternative:* keep the host name and strip only `.lan`: one more suffix list that the next network breaks. **(2) One Done today.** **今天做完 / Done today** counts the tasks that finished well (`done`) at a moment on today's local day; a failed task, a `done_claimed` and a wait that ended unmet (**没等到 / Didn't happen**, D145) are listed in the Done today section with their own words and never counted; nor is an ended call. It starts on its first trigger, and at boot when it has run before (so a restart picks up what it was in the middle of); idle, it parks itself like the default. *Its words:* an L1 identity of its own (`otherIdentity`): its name, and that the person has other partners whose conversations it never sees, so it never claims to and never speaks as them. *Routing (the ~36 writes):* every core module still writes to `channel`; with more than one partner the Log's append routes a write that belongs to another partner to that partner's conversation, by what it is about: a task (its card's persona), a question, a wait, a call, a routine or a note whose first event was in that partner's conversation (decisionId, waiterId, callId, routineId, noteId, rebuilt from the Log at start), or a write made while core handles that partner's tool call (`actAs`, AsyncLocalStorage, set by the MCP hub). An answer always lands beside its question. Triggers go the same way: another partner's conversation, task, wait or routine wakes that partner, never the default. **Stay the default's:** proactive notes (finds), the first words, chat apps (Telegram, Slack, iMessage), Bridge, the home's own questions (a computer closing, Mem's plugin, Reach from outside), forgetting and the trusted agents in Settings › 伙伴. *Tasks and routines carry their partner from creation:* a task the partner opens carries its persona (as before); a New task or a routine made in another partner's conversation is that partner's (`RoutineBody.persona`); a routine's runs are its partner's tasks. *MCP:* one hub, a partner role per partner (token `partner:<id>`); tools a partner registers are its own (the default's are untouched), core's shared tools serve each with its persona in the call; `log_read`, `log_search` and `task_read` keep to the caller's own (another's conversation or task is out of reach, a wide search keeps only its own); a task's calls carry its partner, so its `memory_search` is its partner's, and its brief names its own partner. *Memory:* its own Mem identity (`ducter-<id>`, never the identity Ducter itself runs with), bound once Mem answers with memory on, kept in its folder's persona.json and set as its tasks' NMEM_AGENT_ID; until bound it neither recalls nor saves. *On hand:* one board as before; with more than one partner each row and card carries its partner's small stone, and another partner's own questions are listed under 等你 / Needs you as **{name} 问你 / {name} asks you** with the question, a click shows that partner (D309's counted-but-not-listed gap closed: the strip, the section and the bar now add the same things). A reply in another partner's conversation quotes within it. *Left:* per-partner settings (how it talks, memory on or off, accounts), its L1 from its own Mem identity's bundle, chat apps per partner, removing a partner, the Mac's rename of another partner, linking partners, Bridge per partner, the comprehension test (`design/personas.md` "What's left"). | U (task brief), D309, D24, D18 | `design/personas.md`, `design/product-model.md` §1, §5, `design/scenarios.md` A5, `design/todo.md` |

## 2026-11-17: a phone task opened early, before its needs were written, had no phone tools (the author's "复测真机借用与外部录屏能力并更新复盘", Codex, on the server home: "ALL_TOOLS 没有任何 phone 工具；phone_look 分派 TypeError")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D316 | **An early task (D120) is kept only when the call's needs are the head's; a task's phone and Mac-app tools follow its latest task_open; a phone tool that can't serve says why in words.** *Found, from code and fakes (not on hel):* D120 opens a task from the streamed head of `task_open` (everything before `brief`). When the model wrote `brief` before `needs`, or the task opened from its title alone, the early task had no `needs`; the call then said `needs.phone: "mine"`, but the match checked only place, agent and model, so the early task was kept: its session started without the phone brief, on a computer picked without the phone, and core read `needs` from the task's **first** `task_open` (cached for its life), so `phone_*` were never listed (D260 lists by need, and the need was empty). The "TypeError" was Codex's own: its tool listing (`ALL_TOOLS`) had no `phone_look`, so a call to it failed inside Codex, not in Ducter. An earlier task that day worked because its head carried `needs`. (1) **The partner** drops the early task and opens it the usual way when the call's needs differ from the head's (like a different place, agent or model); the ack stays one. (2) **Core** (`android/index.ts`, `computer/index.ts`) reads needs from the task's latest `task_open` and forgets its cached answer on each new one (a briefed open, a move, a rename all state it again). (3) **Words:** a phone tool refused because the task can't use a phone says which reason (its work wasn't opened as phone work; it isn't working; no phone is ready: none of the user's is lent through 用这台手机 and Ducter's phone isn't set up on that computer), then "Report blocked in one line saying so"; a fault inside a phone tool (a TypeError) reaches the task as "failed inside Ducter … nothing was done on the phone", never as a bare JavaScript error. A task whose work needs a phone but has no `phone_*` tools already reports blocked by its brief (D247), so the person reads why on the task. *Not taken:* listing the phone tools for every task (thirteen more tools in every session, and a phone for work that never asked for one). | the author, 2026-11-17 | `packages/partner/src/partner.ts`, `packages/partner/test/ack-and-go.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/android/{index,tools}.ts`, `packages/core/src/computer/index.ts`, `packages/core/test/handset-which.test.ts` |

The home makes it once from the stream (pages of 5,000 by its (stream, seq) index) and then adds each event the Log appends (`core/src/session-index.ts`, the 64 tasks asked about last); `task_index` answers it, or its turns from `fromSeq` on after a new socket; each client adds live events with the same `indexAdd` (both ports pass `fixtures/transcript.json`'s `index`). 50,000 events: 2,084 turns, 351 KB (about 7 KB per 1,000 events, gzipped with D284's frames), made in 5 ms. **(2) A window both ways.** The page lays out every turn of the index; a client holds at most `WINDOW.keep` 1,500 events around what is on screen plus always the newest `WINDOW.tail` 200 (what the rest of the app reads), letting go when it holds 300 more (`keepFor`: two thirds of what it keeps lie ahead of the scroll); `nextAsk` asks one page of 300 at a time, the turns on screen first, then 600 events ahead of the scroll and 300 behind, growing the stretch next to them (`task_history` `beforeSeq`, or the new `afterSeq` for a far stretch growing down) or, with nothing near, starting 100 events before the turn. A task nobody has open keeps its newest 2,000. D284's background pages up to 2,000 are gone where the home sends an index (kept for a home before D320). The place is kept by the first turn on screen (the Mac's `ui.List` by key; the web by that turn's place in the content), so a page landing or leaving never moves what is read; a reader at the end stays at the end. **(3) Turns built one at a time.** `slotsOf` gives every turn of the index; a turn is built from its own held events, with what it needs from before it (`BuildCtx`: the brief said, the latest report, the event before, more after), only when it is drawn or read, and kept until its events change; a page or a live event builds only its own turns; a turn with nothing held is a blank of the index's height; a turn of more than 1,000 events is built from its newest. Built alone, every turn equals building everything at once (the fixtures), except that the app a run of browser steps is in no longer carries from the turn before. **(4) Drawn only near the screen.** The Mac's list already builds only rows in view; the web now draws the turns within a screen of the view and two spacers (`vlist.ts`), heights measured once drawn, else the index's. **(5) The locator from the index:** the whole session on the rail and in the list; a click on a turn not held goes there at once, its blank first, and tints when it lands; a near one keeps D284's glide. D279's count of wakes is the whole session's. **(6) Huge items:** a text over 20,000 characters (an output, a command or a note over 8,000) is cut before its keys are hidden and drawn; **显示全部（{n} 字）/ Show all ({n} characters)** opens the whole, read from its event, as plain text (the web in the browser's own view, the Mac in the file viewer). **Numbers** (before → after; the web's are its work per step in Bun, the Mac's frames in the test renderer; link 80 ms + 4 Mbit/s, gzipped): *open to first paint*: web 23 → 14–18 ms after the frames (≈ 110–175 ms on the link), Mac 57–63 → 60–61 ms, the same at every size. *Scroll from the end to the head*: web each older page 186 ms (2k), 912 ms (10k), 576 ms and rising (50k: never reached the head) → p95 6–7 ms, longest under 50 ms (headless Chrome, 50k: frame p95 18 ms, no long tasks, at most 15 turns in the page); Mac p95 4.6 ms (2k), 570 ms (10k), did not reach the head in 15 min (50k) → 17–18 ms at every size. *Held*: every event loaded (10,000, 50,000, no limit) → at most 2,000 on both. *Jump into the middle*: before, only after loading everything up to it → web 134 ms to the turn on the link (about 50 ms of work over 4 pages), Mac 44 ms (10k), 143 ms (50k). *Live events while scrolled up*: 2.4 ms p95 each, the reader's turns not rebuilt. *Tradeoff:* the Mac at 2,000 events scrolls at 18 ms p95 where it was 4.6 ms, because a turn is now built as it comes into view and hiding keys in its outputs is most of that; a faster redaction is in todo. *Alternative not taken:* keep everything loaded and only virtualize drawing (memory still grows without bound and every page still rebuilt the transcript). | U (the author, 2026-11-17); ## 2026-11-17: one partner, one mailbox, one home answering it; the live trial as its own identity (the author: "bridge 你第一性原理用长期有价值的方式去决定吧"; research/66 §9)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D324 | **Built 2026-11-17 with fakes only (core, protocol, web, Mac, the trial script); nothing was created on the person's Mem; not reviewed by the author; no persona or tool change, so no eval.** *Found:* the live trial stopped because Mem lists two active connections for `ducter`, both labelled `ducter`: hel's Ducter (connected from Settings) and the Mac's own nmem login, connected by hand for the 2026-11-13 trial (the Mac's `~/.ducter` has no `bridge-connection.json`, so no Ducter there reads it; its `ducter` context is the trial's). Whoever reads first takes a message, so one of the person's agents' requests can land where nobody looks, and `connections list` can't say which computer is which. *First principles:* the address is **who** (the partner, D18: one Mem identity, `ducter`, or D312's `ducter-<id>`), the connection is **where** (the home it lives on). A mailbox has exactly one reader, so a partner has exactly one home answering it. A Mem identity per home was rejected: it splits the partner's memory and provenance (D141 binds one identity per partner), and a terminal agent would find two "Ducter"s to choose between; two homes that each want their own address are two partners (D312), each with its own identity. **(1) A connection is owned by one home and named for it.** The context Ducter connects with (Mem shows it as the connection's label) is `<identity>-on-<home>-<key tag>`: the home's name as a slug and six hex of its D293 key fingerprint (two Macs both called "mac" still differ), then `-2`… after a revoked one (Mem never reopens a revoked connection by its old name). `DUCTER_BRIDGE_CONTEXT` still overrides it. A connection made before D324 keeps its name and keeps working; nothing is renamed behind the person's back. **(2) A second home never connects beside the first on its own.** Every look reads Mem's list for the identity (read-only). Another home's active connection: the row is **elsewhere**, **{name} 现在在 {home} 上收你别的 AI 发来的消息，这台不用再收。 / {name} gets your other AI agents' messages on {home} now; this computer doesn't need to.** with one action, **改由这台收 / Receive here instead**, which asks in place (**改由这台收？{home} 上就不再收了…**) and on the Go connects here first, then revokes the other (never a moment with nobody answering). A plain Connect there runs nothing. A client (the Mac app or the phone showing a server home) never has a connection of its own: Bridge belongs to the home's core. **(3) Two readers already (from before D324): one calm row, one action.** Under the connected head: **{name} 也在 {home} 上收 / {name} also receives on {home}** (a label from before D324: **另一台电脑 / another computer**), **两台都在收，你别的 AI 发来的消息会被先查收的那台拿走，可能落到你不看的那边。只留一台就好。**, **只留这台 / Keep only this one**, asking in place (**只留这台？{home} 上的 {name} 就不再收你别的 AI 发来的消息了。**). Mem's revoke is "one own connection": one another login made may be refused from here; then the row says **{home} 上的连接只能在那台上断开：在那台的 Ducter 里打开 设置 › 连上的 AI agent，点「断开」。** and offers nothing it can't do. A home whose connection another home ended notices at its next look or its 30-minute recheck (read-only `connections list`), drops its record, and its checks stop. **(4) Per partner (D312), the same rule:** `ducter-work`'s connection is `ducter-work-on-hel-<tag>`; Bridge per partner is still D312's "Left". **(5) The live trial is its own identity** (`bridge-trial.ts`): `--real` makes `ducter-trial-<yyyymmddhhmm>-<hex>` (a ledger under the evidence folder first; `agents enroll … --source-app ducter-trial`; `connections connect`; a check that Mem lists exactly that one active connection), tells the peer that exact contact, runs S1, S2, S3, X1, and removes all of it (revoke, `agents context clear` with its revision, `agents delete --yes`); a failed removal keeps its ledger for `--cleanup`; only an id of the trial's shape is ever removed. The person's `ducter` is never named. So the trial runs any time, whatever the person has connected, and D258's shared-mailbox guard and `--share-mailbox` are retired. **(6) Upstream, drafts only** (research/66 §9.3, not posted): a host or device label (and `created_at`, `last_seen_at`) on each connection, set at `connect`; whether `revoke` may end a connection of the same member made by another login, and its code when not; `outcome_unknown` as a contract (`false` means not admitted, on every verb, `connect` included); what `agents delete` does to a mailbox and its messages. *Tradeoff:* one more read (`connections list`) per look and every 30 minutes. *Alternative not taken:* a Mem identity per home (`ducter-hel`), which needs no coordination but splits who the partner is. | the author, 2026-11-17; D18, D141, D205, D258, D293, D312 | `design/bridge.md` "One home answers (D324)", "Try it live"; `design/product-model.md` glossary; `design/roadmap.md`; `design/todo.md`; `docs/settings.md`; `research/66` §9; `packages/core/src/{bridge-link,core,ws,main}.ts`; `packages/protocol/src/index.ts`; `packages/partner/eval/{bridge-trial,bridge-live,fake-bridge-nmem}.ts`; `packages/core/test/{bridge-homes,bridge-link}.test.ts`; `packages/partner/test/bridge-trial.test.ts`; `apps/web/src/{memory.tsx,app.ts,i18n-memory.ts}`; `apps/desktop/internal/{protocol/protocol.go,views/{peers_pane,app,bridge_test}.go,i18n/memory.go}` |

## 2026-11-17: the partner's own iMessage, step by step (D323; the author, connected in Message yourself: "我不知道给 ducter 单独注册 iMessage 要怎么操作，给自己发体验差，每一个消息有两遍")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D323 | **Built 2026-11-17 on the Mac (bridge and Settings), the protocol, the core and the web's Chat apps page; checked by tests with fakes (a fake store, sender and host, a fixture `chat.db` with and without `destination_caller_id`, a fake home socket) and in the Mac test renderer's shots (`.shots/d323/`, nine states, zh and en); not seen live: no Apple ID was made, no second macOS user, no real Messages read or iMessage sent.** *Who:* the consumer user and the author alike, who chose 给自己发信息 because the recommended mode gave no way in; the fresh user, who has never made an Apple ID for anything but themselves. *Feel:* before, a recommended mode with one line ("make it an Apple ID") and nothing to do next, and a working fallback where every message shows twice; after, four steps on the card saying what to do on which device, a check that says what this Mac's Messages is signed in to, and an honest line about what each mode is like. *First time:* Settings › 聊天软件 › iMessage, the mode already on the partner's own Apple ID, the steps under it. **(1) What is possible (research/114).** One Apple ID in Messages per macOS user, which may differ from iCloud's. A second macOS user can't carry the partner: AppleScript sending fails while that user is in the background, it must be logged in by hand after every restart, and FileVault (on by default) rules out automatic login; Ducter doesn't offer it and says so when it finds itself there. The self thread's two bubbles are Messages' and can't be removed: Message yourself stays, described honestly. **(2) The recommended paths.** *One Mac:* if the person doesn't use Messages on this Mac themselves, sign **only Messages** in to the partner's Apple ID (iCloud stays theirs, their iMessages stay on their phone): a clean one-to-one thread. If they do, Message yourself, with the cost said. *A spare Mac (an old MacBook, a Mac mini) or a server home with a Mac:* Ducter on that Mac, connected to the home like any Mac, its Messages signed in to the partner's Apple ID, kept awake and logged in; iMessage is connected there. The bridge already lives in the Mac app as a client of the home (D277), so nothing else is needed on that Mac. **(3) The guided setup** (partner mode, before Connect), four steps in D283's step marks: **给{name}注册一个 Apple ID。** (a new email, any device, the codes to the person's own phone; **打开 account.apple.com**); **在这台 Mac 上，让「信息」登录{name}的 Apple ID。** (Messages › Settings › iMessage, only Messages changes) with **检查 / Check**, which asks Messages (macOS asks once for Automation) and says **「信息」登录的是 {address}。** in the done ink, or that it isn't signed in, or, when that address is also this macOS user's iCloud Apple ID, **…和这台 Mac 的 iCloud 是同一个 Apple ID。如果它是你自己的，先在「信息」里换成{name}的。**; **让这台 Mac 一直开着，Ducter 也开着。** (plugged in, awake, someone logs in after a restart; on a Mac where the person uses Messages, use another Mac), which says in the failed ink when this macOS user is in the background; **点「连上」，再用你的手机给{name}的 Apple ID 发一串数字。** Under the choice, the comparison: **一对一的对话，像在跟朋友发消息。要给{name}注册一个 Apple ID，还要一台你自己不用「信息」的 Mac。** and **现在就能用。但每句话在对话里都会出现两遍，一遍是发出的，一遍是收到的：这是「信息」自己的样子，Ducter 改不了。** The old one-line mode notes are gone. **(4) The code tells the truth.** The bridge reads which of this Messages' addresses a message came in at (`destination_caller_id`, else `account`, else nothing, remembered per database). In partner mode, the code arriving in the thread of an address with itself means this is the person's own Apple ID: no one is linked, nothing is sent, and the card says **你发的数字出现在你和自己的对话里：这台 Mac 的「信息」登录的是你自己的 Apple ID。…** with **改成给自己发信息**, which starts over in Message yourself with a fresh code. A code that links learns the partner's address: the code line then says **用你的手机给 {address} 发这串数字：** and the linked row **{name}用 {address} 和你一对一地聊。…** **(5) Which Mac carries it.** `channel_status` carries the Mac's Computer Name; the home adds the Macs carrying iMessage to the Chat apps frame (`imessage`, `here` for the receiving socket), sent again whenever a bridge changes or its socket goes. Another Mac's Settings says **开着，在「{Mac}」上** with **在「{Mac}」上收发** and no Connect (two Macs on one Apple ID would both answer); the web's iMessage group says the same instead of only "set up on a Mac". *Tradeoff:* the steps are words with one check, not an automated sign-in: Ducter never signs in to an Apple ID for the person. *Alternative:* a second macOS user with a SIP-off helper (what other gateways do for background users), ruled out by D277. *Unverified until a live run:* what Messages' account `description` returns (taken to be the address, dropped when it isn't shaped like one), `destination_caller_id` on macOS 26, a new Apple ID getting iMessage on a Mac at the first try | the author (2026-11-17), research/114 | `apps/desktop/internal/imessage/{bridge,chatdb,account,host}.go`, `apps/desktop/imessage.go`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/{imessage,imessage_setup}.go`, `apps/desktop/internal/i18n/imessage.go`, `apps/desktop/internal/protocol/protocol.go`, `packages/protocol/src/{index,channels}.ts`, `packages/core/src/ws.ts`, `apps/web/src/{channels.tsx,i18n-channels.ts}`, `design/{imessage,product-model,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/imessage.md` |

## 2026-11-17: the locator lists the session's landmarks, and talking to a task while it works says what happens (D325; the author: "这个 mini map 最好能选择最近的其他 title 跳转" and "具体 task 发消息那里，怎么设计的 queue 和 steer 的机制和 ui？")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D325 | **Built 2026-11-17 on the web (wide and phone) and the Mac, with the protocol, runner and core; checked with unit tests on both clients, Mac view tests and shots in the test renderer, and headless Chrome against the demo core (`DEMO_LONG=50000`, `DEMO_STEER=1`), zh and en, light and dark (`.shots/d325/locator`, `.shots/d325/composer`); not live on a real agent's steer echo, not reviewed by the author.** **Part 1, the locator.** *Who:* the developer with a loop running for days (before: a hover showed the brief and "等到了 26 次 10:46–10:32", nothing to find a round by; after: every round that reported reads as what it found); the consumer and the fresh user (hover the rail, as before). *Felt:* 好用, 放心. (1) **The locator lists the session's landmarks**, made from the session index alone (`packages/protocol/src/landmarks.ts`, its Go port, `fixtures/landmarks.json`): each said turn, each report (its first line, now carried by the index's mark with its time, `IndexMark.at`/`w`, cut at 120 with keys hidden), each compaction, switch, move or interruption, and between them each run of quiet turns once; a round that reports is its report. Rows are one height and only those near the list's view are drawn (50,000 events: 1,250 landmarks, about 25 rows drawn, made in under 1 ms). Pointing at the rail chooses the landmark nearest that turn and centers the list on it, those in view marked; a click pins it and gives it the keys (↑↓, Page, Home/End; Return goes there by D284's glide or D320's jump; Esc closes); unpinned it closes 260 ms after the pointer leaves. (2) **Times in order:** an item's time alone today, with its day otherwise; a range always earlier first, both days when it crosses one (**昨天 22:10–今天 1:05**), one time within a minute; never "10:46–10:32" (it was a loop across midnight with no day). *Not taken:* a minimap of the rendered page (its cost grows with the session; it says nothing a fresh user can read). **Part 2, the composer while it works.** *Who:* the developer steering several agents (before: Return steered and nothing ever said whether it was read; 做完再说 handed the words to the agent's own queue, where they could not be changed or taken back, shown as a dashed 排队中 bubble mid-transcript), the consumer (wants to know it was heard), the fresh user (should not need the words steer or queue). *Felt:* 放心 and 顺滑: what Return will do is said before it is pressed, and what happened after. *First time:* type while it works; the placeholder says it. (3) **Idle, Return sends** the next turn. **While it works, Return steers** (placeholder **插一句，它做到下一步就会看到… / Add something; it sees it at its next step…**; hint **回车：它做到下一步就会看到** and **⌥ 回车：这一轮做完再说**; on a phone the placeholder stays **直接跟它说…** and the hint says it). (4) **A steer says when it was read:** the runner keeps it unread until the agent's own echo of it comes (OAR's `user_message`: Claude Code's replay with `--replay-user-messages`, Codex's userMessage item, pi's and DeepSeek Harness's user message; mapped to `user_echo` by the normalizer; matched by its words, and every steer before it counts as read), then logs `raw.read`; under the bubble **它做到下一步就会看到 / It'll see this at its next step** with a working dot while unread, **✓ 它看到了 / Seen** on the newest one read, nothing else. (5) **After this is held by Ducter, not the agent:** the runner holds the person's words (`task_held`, the whole queue on each change; `TaskCard.held`, so every window shows it and a restart keeps it); chips over the composer under **这一轮做完再说 / After this turn**, in order: a click edits one in place (**改好了 / 取消**), **现在就说 / Say it now** steers it in (or starts the turn when idle), **× 不说了 / Take back** drops it (`task_held` frame; one already gone: **这句已经发给它了**). When a turn ends completed, everything held is the next turn, each logged as the person's words in order; after a Stop, a failure, a limit or a compaction it stays held; a send while idle carries it first. The partner's and Ducter's own queued words still use the agent's queue. (6) **An agent that can't steer** (`HarnessInfo.steer`, Go `protocol.NoSteer`): Return holds too, and it says so (**{agent} 做事时不能插话，发出的话会等这一轮做完**, chips' head **{agent} 这一轮做完就会看到**, no 做完再说 or 现在就说 while it works). Per OAR 0.95.1's source, all four steer: Claude Code (stream-json user message written into the running turn), Codex (app-server `turn/steer`), pi (SDK `steer`), DeepSeek Harness (bridge `steer`); OAR's withdraw exists for Claude Code, pi and DeepSeek Harness but not Codex, which is why Ducter holds the queue itself. *Alternative not taken:* OAR's own queue with `withdraw` (no edit or take-back on Codex, and the queue would not survive a restart or show in every window). *Also:* `channels-wechat.test.ts` compared WeChat's reply window to the wall clock instead of the rig's fake clock and failed from today; it reads the rig's clock now; `learned-week.test.ts` steps a week of the fake clock a minute at a time and gets 60 s. | U (the author, 2026-11-17); D207, D268, D271, D284, D315, D320; OAR 0.95.1 source | `packages/protocol/src/{index,internal,harnesses,landmarks,session}.ts`, `packages/protocol/fixtures/{landmarks-cases.ts,landmarks.json,transcript.json}`, `packages/runner/src/{runner,normalize}.ts`, `packages/runner/test/{runner,normalize}.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/{ws,registry}.ts`, `packages/core/test/{idempotent-send,channels-wechat,learned-week}.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/{app,store,views,transcript,format,onhand,i18n-transcript}.ts(x)`, `apps/web/static/{app.css,app.js}`, `apps/web/{demo,demo-steer}.ts`, `apps/web/test/{held,locator-list}.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/{protocol/{protocol,session}.go,store/store.go,i18n/{turns,loop,when}.go}`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/{held,landmarks,task,taskturns,taskpage,session,app}.go` and their tests, `design/{focus-window,ui,product-model,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/getting-started.md` **Held words after a Stop stay held (author, 2026-11-17):** a Stop means "let me think again", so nothing the person held goes out on its own; they go when the person sends again or taps 现在就说. |

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |

| D328 | **Built 2026-11-17; the echo checked live on Claude Code (haiku), Codex (gpt-6-luna) and pi (MiniMax-M3) through OAR, DeepSeek Harness by OAR's source only (not installed); not reviewed by the author.** *Who:* the developer steering a task (before: the receipt matched the agent's echo by its words, so an echo whose words the agent's side had changed, or two steers alike, could mark the wrong one; after: the same receipt, matched exactly); the screen-reader user on a wide window (before: the locator was named for what was said, but it lists reports and marks too). *Felt:* 放心. (1) **When Seen shows is unchanged**, because live it is already right: each agent echoes at the step its model takes the words in (Claude Code and pi when the tool call they had already chosen ends; Codex at its next sampling, even while a shell runs under its exec cell). A rule holding the echo until running tools end was tried and dropped: on Codex it showed Seen about 8 s late. Seen means read, not obeyed (one Codex run of three read the steer and kept to the brief). (2) **Matched by id:** the runner mints a UUID per steer and passes it as OAR's `inputId` (`HarnessSession.send`'s `inputId`, carried to a worker); the normalizer keeps the echo's `inputId` in `user_echo`; `steerSeen` finds the steer by id, else by its words (pi, which echoes no id; a worker before this change). Claude Code's `uuid` and Codex's `clientId` came back exactly the id passed. (3) **The locator's name** (its rail and card, Mac and web) is **这件事的经过 / What happened in this task** (was **这件事里说过的话 / What was said in this task**): literal, and true of what D325 made it list. *Alternative not taken:* **跳到这件事里的某一处 / Jump to a point in this task** (names the act, but a list read aloud should say what it holds). | D325, research/116 | `packages/protocol/src/internal.ts`, `packages/runner/src/{runner,normalize,oar,remote,worker-host}.ts`, `packages/runner/test/{runner,normalize}.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/i18n-transcript.ts`, `apps/web/static/app.js`, `apps/desktop/internal/i18n/loop.go`, `design/{focus-window,product-model,todo}.md`, `research/{116-steer-live,README}.md` |
